covenants.name: Laniena
covenants.notes:
History. About a century ago a dead magus's vampire hunted out dhampirs, saw them schooled as hunters, then slew them so they would rise as vampires; House Tremere has suffered vampire infiltration after a dhampir magus's death more than once, and now forbids its magi to take dhampir apprentices. The famous hunter Murat of Terezin came to Coeris then, and with Radomir of Tremere cleared the House of every vampire, Murat killing the nest's master himself. The two asked the Tribunal for an oppidum to train hunters, and once Murat had joined House Ex Miscellanea the Praeco agreed.

The founders. Murat brought initiation scripts set down by a Gnostic scholar who had spied on a taltós clan for months; after years of trials he and Radomir learnt to Open a Gifted person to the Hunters' Arts. Radomir named them interfectores, slayers, soon shortened to Fectores. Radomir, a gifted young idealist, studied the necromancers called the Disciples of the Worm, whom he took for heirs of the Dacian necromancers who served Tremere, and his lore of ghosts and the walking dead fitted Murat's lore of vampires. Murat had found that the Arts work on more than vampires. Murat of Terezin trained three apprentices, the first Hermetic Fectores, a new societas of House Ex Miscellanea; the youngest, also named Murat, lives here.

The law. Some magi say training a Gifted child as a Fector makes a delinquent master, since the child is kept from the Hermetic Arts. Laniena answers that trainees are not yet of the Order, so the Code does not protect them, and that each is offered the Order's protection as soon as trained, as Join or Die demands. The Tribunal, that is House Tremere, lets it go on, but could at any time accuse it of the High Crime of robbing a magus of his power.

Hermetic Fectores take one Practice Art as their free Major non-Hermetic Virtue with its Foe Art, a Minor Magical Focus in harming one kind of creature as their free Minor Hermetic Virtue, and Weak Spontaneous Magic as their Major Hermetic Flaw. The Foe Arts the Fectores hold so far are five: Vampire, Werewolf, Ghost, Nightwalker and Witch. Murat's scripts can Open the Hunters' Arts or teach a new Foe Art, but hold nothing for the Practice Arts alone, so no unGifted Fector can be trained.

Covenfolk: a band of elite warriors trained to fight under a Fector's command; Bendis is the ablest of the non-Hermetic Fectores. The book gives no founding year (soon after the purge of about a century ago) and no season.

Story seeds: a character may be one of Murat of Terezin's children, doomed to slay her own father; and if Lexander learns that Murat the Younger has let a vampire live, House Tremere's anger could fall on the whole oppidum.
covenants.summary:
The 'slaughterhouse': an oppidum at the mouth of Baradla Cave, the largest of the Aggtelek caves in northern Hungary, whose business is training the Fectores, House Tremere's hunters of supernatural foes, who use non-Hermetic Hunters' Arts drawn from the native magic of the Balkans. House Tremere counts the experiment a success. It began as part of the Scholomance and moved here when it became an oppidum of its own.

A few solid houses lean against a tall half-moon wall across the cave mouth, and a dense hedge of black hawthorn, grown on purpose, rings the homes of the magi and covenfolk. Inside are an arena, smithies and carpenters' shops, a chirurgeon and an apothecary's laboratory.

Two of every three Gifted youngsters found or sent here are trained as Fectores, five years under a Fector with Scry, Ban and Slay and three Foe Arts, and then join the Order as Gifted companions of House Ex Miscellanea; the other third become Murat's Hermetic apprentices, Hermetic Fectores. House Tremere forbids Hermetic training for dhampirs, who may still become Fectores. Trainees who prove unreliable never swear the Oath or learn Parma, and are spent on the most dangerous fronts. The Fectores serve House Tremere first, which makes some magi wonder what they are really for.

Its two magi are the filii of its two founders and, unlike them, are always at odds. Anyone keen on the Hunters' Arts is welcome to join.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: Baradla Cave, Imaginem and Muto
Vis: Dobsinska Cave, Ignem
Vis: Ochtinska Cave, Rego (the flowers of iron, also lesser enchantment vis)
Library: Murat of Terezin's initiation scripts for the Hunters' Arts, which Murat the Younger keeps from Lexander
Services: trained Fectores for House Tremere, three in the time one apprentice takes
Boon: Hedge Tradition (the Fectores)
Boon: Veteran Fighters (elite warriors trained to fight under a Fector)
Hook: Superiors (House Tremere, on whose sufferance it exists)
Hook: Hermetic Politics (whether training Gifted children outside the Order is lawful)
Hook: Dark Secret (Murat of Terezin's undeath)
Tension: Lexander against Murat the Younger, over the scripts and the training
covenants.secrets:
Murat of Terezin was secretly a dhampir himself. On his death he rose as a vampire, and has lasted long enough to become a kukudhi, a vampire that passes as human (see the Bestiary). He lives far from Laniena with his fourth mortal wife and has fathered more than twenty children, every one a dhampir.
Only Murat the Younger knows. He lets the vampire be, because it gives the Fectores a steady stream of Faerie-blooded hunters and has given at least one Gifted child.

covenants.name: Evredika
covenants.notes:
The book gives no season, and no single aura for an oppidum spread over many sites; the Devil's Throat's 4 is used. Three of its six magi are unnamed.

Story seed: a hunting party led by a noble with a tame white wolf strips all of Evredika's vis sources, and Gigas, the Tremere's ill-hidden cat's paw in the Theban Tribunal, seems the obvious thief. If its protests are honest, who is framing Gigas, and why?
covenants.summary:
The oppidum of the Cult of Orpheus, a societas of House Ex Miscellanea, spread across the Rhodope Mountains to guard the places of Orpheus's legend, and named for his lost love Eurydice in her Bulgarian form. Its magi live alone in caves, strong houses and hidden towers and seldom visit one another, meeting once a year in a meadow near Gela when the silivriak is in flower. Its sites are Gela, the Devil's Throat, Perperikon and the Rock Womb.

When the Cult joined the Order, its two holiest places, on Lesbos and in the Rhodopes, came into the Hermetic world; the Rhodope cult, decades old by then, became an oppidum in 1001. Its five Orphic magi are foederati; the sixth is the aedile, always a Tremere, whom the House takes care to pick for respect for the Cult's ways and some love of music. Oeagrus drives most of them to ask for a new posting within about ten years.

Approaches to the Theban Tribunal, where Evredika might seem to belong, met scorn from the Theban Jerbiton, who think its music a peasant's jig and its paganism an offence; its magi would rather House Tremere ignored them than House Jerbiton sneered.

By the old Orphic rule women may not enter the cult's holy places and stay in the oppidum's unconsecrated buildings.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: Imaginem from the year's first silivriak flowers
Vis: Corpus, bone fragments washed up in the Devil's Throat (now and then)
Vis: a yearly grant to the teacher at Gela (a Personal Vis Source)
Aura: Magic 4 at the Devil's Throat, 3 at Perperikon
Library: no books named
Hook: Contested Resource (its vis, which Gigas has been told not to contest)
Hook: Superiors (the Tremere aedile the House posts there)
Tension: Oeagrus and each Tremere aedile, Yekaterina most of all
Tension: the Cult on Lesbos, which Oeagrus thinks hides Orpheus's head
covenants.secrets: Oeagrus keeps the mummified arm of Orpheus and means to remake the god by grafting his scattered limbs onto his own body.

covenants.name: Seuthopolis
covenants.notes:
The book gives no season or founding year. Of its fourteen magi eight are unnamed: four younger Guernicus and four lictors.

Lictors: hoplites sworn to long service, who guard the Quaesitors and do as they say. Here a lictor may claim reasonable help from any cives, socius, foederatus or colona, the Tribunal judging afterwards how much was reasonable by how great and how near the danger was. All the Tribunal's lictors belong to the same body, so all wear the same red and silver sash on formal occasions, fastened with a silver brooch called an astraea, usually enchanted: at least three inches long, a pair of wings spread from a forked lightning bolt, each with its own mark. Saturnino's is set in a six-inch oval studded with gems in the pattern of Virgo. Carrying a copy of a lictor's badge is a serious crime. The mediation and domestic teams' lictors change often, most serving three years; Terencia and Saturnino stay longer. The unnamed hoplites are mostly Tremere, but the Prima has lately moved some of them to Lycaneon, which leaves room for player characters.

The townsfolk are Greeks, Bulgars and mountain Slavs who went where the wars of the other two could not easily reach them; the town has bowed to Byzantine and Bulgarian crowns in turn and is, with the Latin Empire so weak, under Bulgaria in name. They are the oppidum folk least shaped by Hermetic service, without the Tremere virtues of loyalty, letters, arms and merit, and with no former Redcaps among them: like many Western covenants it is staffed by people who fled the world for a different life, and the Quaesitors find their skills, some a little shady, useful.
covenants.summary:
A walled town at the Tribunal's southern edge and the base of its Quaesitors and hoplites, on the border with the Theban Tribunal, where its magi fairly well keep the two Tribunals' quarrels from turning into raids across the line. It also looks after the Tribunal's meeting place in the Shipka Pass nearby.

Seuthopolis was the Thracian capital when Rome came, ruled by a priest king of underworld gods whose rites Rome stamped out. A small sect of Verditius magi revived them in a Theban covenant, the Covenant of the Four Divinities, always two senior Verditius and two juniors (one now and then of another House), four being a holy number to the Cabeiri cult. After some friction its members came over to Transylvania as foederati. Over the centuries the cult faded and the oppidum became the Tribunal's seat of justice.

House Guernicus forbids its members to worship the old Thracian gods: three of the House have been removed from office for irrational conduct, and the cult seems the thread linking them. Its initiates take on hubris, as Verditius magi do, and with it a taste for vendettas.

Outwardly it is an ordinary small Bulgarian walled town, owing homage to no lord. Local nobles know nobody has ever taken it, and that those who tried died in ghastly, wondrous ways; the Quaesitors observe that no neighbouring lord has been melted into a puddle of boiling gold since they took over, being subtler than the Verditius, but the tales live on. The magi and their people live about the town in houses like rich merchants'.

Eight Guernicus magi live here with six lictors. Benilda, the leader, keeps research, enchanting and Hermetic law for herself, and sends Vigilia to look into crimes within oppida, Scipio to mediate between oppida, and Caledonia to punish or to investigate by force, each with two lictors and a young Guernicus. For safety only two of the three teams are ever out at once.

In other Tribunals crimes fall between covenants; here, where magi share oppida, they happen within them, and centuries of puzzling over how to investigate magi who live side by side have made these Quaesitors pioneers of their House's Transitionalist movement. Mediation is a common alternative to a case at Tribunal, where the Tremere always win but make enemies doing it.
covenants.what_matters:
Aura: Magic 5 in the caverns; the vault of the libraries is Divine 3
Library: the Red and Black Libraries, Benilda's charge
Boon: Hidden Resources (laboratories and libraries in the caverns beneath the town)
Boon: Prestige (no lord has ever taken the town, and the locals know it)
Hook: Hermetic Politics (Transitionalist against Traditional Guernicus)
Hook: Superiors (House Guernicus; the lictors serve House Tremere too)
Duty: keeps the Shipka Pass Tribunal site and calls the yearly Tribunals
Tension: the Valley of the Thracian Kings, which Benilda holds closed against House Tremere
Tension: the Red and Black Libraries, which many think should be burnt
Tension: the old cult of the Cabeiri, banned to Guernicus
covenants.secrets:
The town's charter from Diocletian is a clever forgery.
Rumour, perhaps true, says the Red Library also holds magic items, seized in investigations and never destroyed, that cast some of the Red Spells; the House might argue they are lawful to own, and lawful to use on hedge wizards, the Orders of Odin and Solomon, and Renounced magi, whom the Code does not protect.
Saturnino thinks gathering the Red and Black Libraries was a grave mistake.

covenants.name: Tablinum
covenants.notes:
The book gives no season. All four magi are named.

Past Curators:
878-900 Akilina, the first, who found the site in the mid-800s, named her apprentice Potitus to follow her, resigned and vanished in 917; presumed dead, though magi as late as 1137 claim to have met her, or someone using her name, in the regiones.
900-948 Potitus, the first to live there, who opened the storehouse to study.
946-1007 Tiberia, a Tremere general named by Potitus and briefly Curator with him; killed in the Schism War.
1007-1018 Anatolus, also a Tremere general and the first chosen by the Tribunal, known for strange battle magic said to come from Tablinum; killed in Wizard's War.
1018-1020 no Curator.
1020-1027 Silus, charged with infernalism and Marched.
1027-1080 Justius, said to have dismantled several Infernal exhibits and driven demons from many levels.
1080-1102 Scribonius, who wrote the first 'complete' catalogue, then resigned, left House Tremere for House Jerbiton in Thebes, and died in 1137.
1102-1170 Calpurnius, who greatly enlarged the Faerie collection.
1170- Nestor, known for his study of regiones.

How so many sealed regiones came to lie here is unknown; they and their Arcane Connections existed by 900, when the Chronicle first mentions them. One story says a ritual path through a labyrinth once led into all of them, and the founders walked it fixing Arcane Connections and destroying the labyrinth behind them.

Laboratories:
Nestor's true laboratory, in an otherwise empty level, used by Curators for centuries: Greater Feature (orrery), Palatial, Extensive Stores, Specimens, Missing Sanctum Marker, Regio, Impregnable, Predecessor; Size +3, Quality +1, Refinement +3, Safety +1, Upkeep +4, Health +2, Warping +2, Aesthetics +4; Experimentation +1, Teaching +2, Rego +2, Vim +3.
Demetrius's: Greater Feature (desk), Specimens (now Aquam, changed in a few days), Studio (where new acquisitions wait), Cramped; Size 0, Quality -1, Refinement +3, Safety 1, Upkeep 0, Health 0, Warping 0, Aesthetics +4; Texts +4, Aquam +1.
Theodora's: Greater Feature (an ever-boiling cauldron), Faerie Ingredients (faerie rocks), Dirty, Disorganized, Chaotic; Size 0, Quality +1, Refinement +2, Safety -1, Upkeep -1, Health -1, Warping +2, Aesthetics -1; Experimentation +6, Muto +2, Perdo +1, Terram +1.
Theodore's: Greater Feature (a still pool), Superior Heating, Flawless Equipment (dwarf-made), Grand Entranceway, Guard, Highly Organized, Spotless, Undecorated; Size 0, Quality +3, Refinement +3, Safety +3, Upkeep +2, Health +2, Warping 0, Aesthetics +6; Vis Extraction +1, Creo +1, Intellego +2, Ignem +1.
The Vim Distillery, shared: Greater Feature (vis still), Lesser Feature (vis balance), Missing Ingredients (Intellego, Muto, Perdo and Rego Lab Totals halved), Superior Equipment, Greater Focus (vis still), Missing Sanctum Marker, Cramped; Size 0, Quality 0, Refinement 0, Safety -1, Upkeep -3, Health 0, Warping 0, Aesthetics +1; Vis Extraction +10.
The Empty Laboratory, stripped and haunted by a magus murdered there in Wizard's War, with a window open on a void: Vis Source, Empty, Undecorated, Abyss, Haunted; Size 0, Quality 0, Refinement 0, Safety -3, Upkeep -1, Health -1, Warping +2, Aesthetics -3; Perdo +1, Mentem +3.
The guest laboratory in the Scriptorium: Gallery, No Stores, Undecorated; all Characteristics 0 save Upkeep -1 and Safety -1; Teaching +1.

Story seed: a Church delegation arrives while the magi study here. Since 1204 the Latins hold much of Constantinople, and scholars there have read in Greek Church records of Tablinum's hoard of relics; a papal legate comes to learn whether it exists and, if so, to take the relics to Rome. Nestor asks the visiting magi to help him deal with it.
covenants.summary:
The Tribunal's museum and storehouse, keeping records, spell texts and artifacts in dozens of regiones in the Danube delta, each hall reached only by Arcane Connection. It was founded in 878, after the Sundering, where so many regiones overlie one another; with the Tribunal held to five covenants it had no standing and no lawful residents, only a place to keep things, until the idea of oppida spread and it remade itself as one, with resident Curators. The Curator holds office for life.

Any Tremere may use the open exhibits, and others usually by the Curator's leave; vandals and thieves, Tremere too, are thrown out for good, at least in theory. Most of the restricted exhibits open to Tremere with good reason and to others now and then, sometimes for a fee. Exhibits are studied as realia, of Source Quality from about 5 (cursory) to 11 or more (unparalleled), lessened when several share one; a rival for an exhibit turns up unless a stress die beats 3, and certamen for love often settles who studies.

Upkeep, checking wards, renewing preserving spells, feeding the Animal exhibit, takes one magus full time, with about a dozen grogs housed in the Scriptorium; the four residents each give it a season a year.

Nestor pays collectors, in vis or access to restricted exhibits (or duplicate objects), for things from a named place or for a named exhibit; grogs and companions are paid in money. Owners, magi among them, may call it theft. Tremere collectors may serve in the vexillation Convectoris-Tablinum.
covenants.what_matters:
Aura: Magic 5 in the Curator's Sanctum; ten listed levels from Infernal 3 to Divine 6
Defence: an Aegis of the Hearth of magnitude 8 round the village palisade
Vis: Vim, extracted from the aura in the shared Vim Distillery (Vis Extraction +10)
Library: the Transylvania Chronicle, the Spell Hall and the exhibits as realia
Boon: Regio (dozens of halls reached only by Arcane Connection)
Boon: Hidden Resources (the Curators' necklaces of Arcane Connections)
Hook: Superiors (the Tribunal appoints the Curator; Tremere has rights of access)
Hook: Contested Resource (rival scholars, and owners of collected objects)
Tension: the Dungeon and the Chapel's relics, which many want destroyed or returned
Tension: Nestor's fear of a Tremere plot against him
covenants.secrets:
The Empty Laboratory's void window is a vis source the residents do not know of: now and then frost forms on its sill that can be gathered as Mentem vis before it melts, 2 pawns a season. The ghost knows.
Nestor keeps most of the Curators' necklaces hidden and carries only the one for the most visited levels; his real laboratory is in a level of its own.
The Dungeon's excess: either infernalists with their own Arcane Connections use it to hide their cult's paraphernalia, coming and going by Leap of Homecoming, or Hell has got in, and possessed exhibits are summoning more demons into the hall.
Theodore once told Nestor many exhibits should be destroyed, and lately told Demetrius the Order has outlived its purpose.

covenants.name: Old Histria
covenants.notes:
Origins. The Incantation of Lightning, usually thought Druidic, was in fact invented here, as a tool for farming.

The Strange Vis. Folk witches break fevers with a potion of the roof tar of a village's four outermost houses. Hermetic scholars found that on Saint John's Eve the tar of the corner houses of seemingly random villages takes on a little Creo vis, so the tar of many villages is gathered and tested every year. Odd enough that it forms only in the Dominion, and only when the four houses' tar is kept unmixed and complete; odder still, it began to appear in Istrian villages once Histria joined, as if it spreads with the Tribunal. Some magi think whatever makes it knows the Tribunal's border; others scoff.

The vis register. Most Transylvanian magi may not sell vis or enchanted items abroad; only the socii, the Praeco, the Tremere Primus, and those acting for them may. Sales need not pass through Old Histria: matching letters, notarised by a Quaesitor, suffice. The Praeco's agents may bid for anything of interest to the Tribunal, which can raise sellers' prices and hurts buyers of rarities, while buyers of common vis can compare the speculative promissory notes on file with Old Histria's vis-trading master. The same bar on sales covers many magical beasts, letting House Tremere, always after breeding stock for war, buy exports first and bid on imports.

Mansiones. Mercere rest houses, a day apart on the main roads between oppida, some secret and for the Order alone, others half-public and open to merchants and clergy. They are not oppida, having no resident cives. Small towns of the founders' descendants have grown round the biggest; since their holders owe the King of Hungary no fealty this is no trouble yet, but some heirs are marrying into the lesser nobility.

The Redcap families. Only Gifted Mercere vote in this Tribunal; in return the Redcaps have been let multiply. An oppidum can have a 'Redcap' each week if it likes; whole families tour as players, carrying messages and swaying the common folk with their plays; retired Redcaps keep businesses in most towns; magi's spouses are sometimes named Redcaps to give them rights under Hermetic law. They think of themselves as one big, fond, odd family of near-magicians, and call each other cousin. House Mercere formally counts only fifteen Redcaps in Transylvania; the Tremere reckon about forty-five are needed (two for each major oppidum, the House's staff, and the retired, trainees and honorary members). The children of several kinds of local vampire make good Redcaps, and the House seeks them out; those not taken become grogs.

Harco. House Mercere has only some 150 members, and the Tremere wish to add thirty-five Transylvanian Redcaps looks to Harco like a lever on the House. The local Mercere side with the Prima, see no reason their children should not all be Redcaps, and are unmoved by a recluse in Piedmont. The present truce: Harco accepts the heads of the Redcap families as members, and the rest as the House's agents, whom Transylvanian magi treat and call Redcaps. The Roman Mercere find the vampire-blooded ones creepy and recognise none of them, and Redcaps proud of heroic blood despise them, though the bloodcaps of the Celtic lands, faerie-blooded themselves, get on with them. If someone on the Roman side pushes for control the truce may fail; player magi could broker a new one.

Stories. The Mercere House's duties are the usual ones (recruiting, training, supporting and rescuing Redcaps), but at this scale whole troupes of players or shiploads of messengers vanish, and every oppidum then gets a formal plea for help that it would be shameful to ignore. New coloniae in interesting country may find a small Mercere school bolted on; trainee Redcaps are always trouble. Histrian magi are the usual envoys to the domus magnae of the west (Harco, Magvillis, Valnastium, the Cave of Twisting Shadows), always at least two, one Tremere and one not; a saga of envoys reaches Autumn covenants, royal courts and Arab, Cuman and Hebrew sorcerers.

The Venice lodging. Three Gifted members live at the chapter house in Venice, in the Roman Tribunal, Merit of Tremere among them; a Mercere's Portal from Old Histria to it has been mooted for years (see the Tribunal's docket).

Vigilia of Seuthopolis may not be given cases touching the Histrian oppida, after her censure. The book gives no founding year and no season. Of the unnamed magi, one is Gifted and in Istria and two are in Venice.
covenants.summary:
The elder of the two Mercere oppida of Istria, and the Tribunal's Mercere House: its gatekeeper to the west, its chief negotiator with foreigners, and a recruiting ground, school and market for the Redcap families. It sits in a much-rebuilt hill fort above Pazin in a Magic aura of 7. House Tremere bases its merchant navy and the Tribunal's diplomats here and at Shrouded Bay; some say the House's spies in the Roman Tribunal are run from here too, which the Tremere deny.

Histria was a covenant of the Roman Tribunal, claiming the whole peninsula through its name. Worn down by that Tribunal's endless politics, its magi came over to Transylvania as foederati, bringing their outpost on Cres with them. The Tribunal has since made the camp, where socii now dominate, the place of record for every sale of vis and enchanted items.

Its members are the same as Shrouded Bay's: eight Gifted magi between the two, three more who live at the chapter house in Venice, and many unGifted Redcaps, who are full members and vote in the oppidum's own ballots. Magi of the two camps often add Adiran, of the Adriatic, to their names, which the swarm of same-named Redcaps makes useful.

It is roomy enough for formal gatherings and for the Redcap families' many projects, but cold and stormy in winter; the strong aura is what keeps researchers there through the sleet.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: the mercury pool, a rich Terram source (a child dipped in it gains Visions and often worse Flaws)
Vis: the truffles of the northern Istrian woods (Herbam), sought by faeries, worth their weight in gold
Vis: the Strange Vis, a little Creo in the roof tar of the four corner houses of random villages on Saint John's Eve, collected Tribunal-wide
Register: the place of record for all sales of vis and magic items in the Tribunal, with the master of vis trading's list of promissory notes
Laboratory: Accursius's suite and excellent laboratory, used by Volante
Library: no books named; the Mercere House's records
Items: the House's cache of magic items, and the potent items guarding the fort
Boon: Aura (Magic 7); Fortified site (a layered hill fort)
Hook: Hermetic Services (the Mercere House: Redcaps, the vis register, the Tribunal's envoys)
Hook: Harsh winters
Tension: Harco recognises few of the Tribunal's Redcaps, and none who are vampire-blooded
Tension: the proposed Mercere's Portal to the Venice chapter house
covenants.secrets: Pahniro's frailty is an act: he was a hoplite for twenty years and has killed three magi in single combat, and he may well be the House's spymaster for the Roman Tribunal.

covenants.name: Shrouded Bay
covenants.notes:
Naval stories. The Adriatic is the safer of the Tribunal's two coasts and one of the world's busiest trade lanes. The fleets have their works here and in a hidden cache somewhere in the southern Dalmatian isles, Leviathan in the Tremere plans (see the hidden fortresses). Trade, piracy and salvage stories can draw on City & Guild. Phillip of Lycaneon, who builds naval parts, is often here tinkering.

The book gives no founding year and no season. One Gifted member is unnamed.
covenants.summary:
The younger Histrian oppidum, a large villa on the Venetian island of Cres, hidden by The Shrouded Glen in a Magic aura of 6. Old Histria's magi set up a chapter house here to guard the island's storm-washed Rego vis, too far from the fort to protect, against raids by Transylvanian Tremere; when Histria joined the Tribunal, the settlement became an oppidum too. In law it stands alone, but the two camps share their members and are close allies.

Most Histrian magi like it better than Old Histria, above all in winter, and Accursius, the chief Mercere, lives here. It holds the support works for the small Mercere and Tremere trading fleets, and its aedile, Placido, runs the Tremere fleet from it.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: the well of blood, a major Corpus source, used for the Redcaps' longevity rituals
Vis: Rego washed up on one beach after storms among ships' wreckage, accruing through the year
Laboratory: Accursius's, less good than his suite at Old Histria
Library: no books named
Fleet: the support base of the Mercere and Tremere trading fleets
Boon: Aura (Magic 6); Hidden (The Shrouded Glen)
Hook: Ruled by Venice
Tension: Leviathan, the secret base in the southern Dalmatian isles, is to be opened if Shrouded Bay seems unsafe in war
Tension: the Grave of Aspytrus and its serpents, on the island

covenants.name: Lycaneon
covenants.notes:
Gold is worth little. Grogs with magic tools mined the mountain's gold out in the oppidum's first decades. The Tremere learned by owning more of it than anyone that gold is only worth what you can spend, and few in Mythic Europe can pay a high price for it; silver spends more easily but floods an economy (as happened lately in Stonehenge), and ruin breeds poverty, and poverty diabolism, so the House now urges laws limiting how much wealth magi may make. Gold is soft and heavy, poor stuff for enchantment; silver at least tempts or repels local faeries, so it can be traded for vis or made into weapons. Few other Houses see it, but the mines ended Tremere's hunger for territory: land is worth only the work of its people, so the House grows by having more magi doing what it wants.

Look and feel. Tremere designed it before Gothic building, so its grandeur is in texture, ornament and size: walls carved with battle scenes, his sayings and Roman motifs, and gold everywhere, which modern Tremere think vulgar. None of his statues is life size: in the Grand Refectory a twelve-foot Tremere rests his hand on a cowed golden dragon. Renovation has never been a priority.

The people. The covenfolk and the little towns around descend from the miners Tremere brought; generations under the House have made them unlike any other folk. They speak a Latin dialect, mostly read and write, and reckon like merchants. Each village elects three leaders, who meet in a council they call a Tribunal over borders, trade and crime, and women often lead. Their fighters are mountain skirmishers with bow, axe and short sword, retired grogs settle among them, and the descendants of the specialists keep their crafts, so many curious wares are made here, which Redcaps carry round the Tribunal.

The wolves. Tremere took the mountain's lead wolf as his familiar, and many of his line seek a white wolf in turn; the House's pack loyalty and shared rearing of the young may have come to him through that bond. The wolves say they descend from men changed in a rite and left in wolf shape when the Oracles fell silent. Now and then a cub is born a throwback, human on summer's first night, its midpoint and its last; trained, such children master the change and serve the House. Wolves who wed humans have children more given than most to nightwalking in wolf shape.

A refuge. Its oversized plan is a relic of the Schism War: it was rebuilt to take the flood of refugees had Diedne won the west, so that magi with no taste for war could still serve it, and every magus on the Tremere side knew a fallen covenant could flee through a Portal to Harco and on to Lycaneon. The House holds that refugees seldom solve the crisis that cost them their home. A troupe that loses its covenant can retreat here, rebuild over years, and go back to retake it.

The book gives no founding year (the Founder's own time) and no season. Nine of the fourteen magi are unnamed.
covenants.summary:
House Tremere's first domus magna, which the Founder meant as a throne to rule the world from and which never was one: since the Sundering, when Tremere moved his seat to Coeris, it has been the House's manufactory, and one of the Order's greatest. It holds the Tribunal's Mercere Portal to Harco, so it is the natural staging post for forces sent to other Tribunals.

It is busiest when war threatens or the House's stores must be rebuilt after one: it was enlarged and filled for decades after the Schism War, and readied nearly a year before the Corruption of Tytalus came out at Tribunal. In peace it holds eight magi; in 1220 it has fourteen, against room for thirty-two, because the Fourth Crusade has weakened the Theban rivals and some magi who would serve as hoplites at Seuthopolis are working here on the Prima's projects. Three are Verditius (two lately hired; the Tremere usually keep one, as Verditius magi chafe at each other) and two are Bonisagus using spare laboratories for original research, who will teach the Tremere any useful breakthrough.

Its long-standing members are informal with one another, by Tremere standards: their work is shared, not competitive, and among the senior Tremere not secret, which suits frank talk about costly, dangerous research. Many Tremere come for a season or more to use its laboratories for a big project.

Archmagus Albertus, the Praeco, runs its work: he assigns projects, sees them done, and deals with magi who want to commission, buy or borrow an item.
covenants.what_matters:
Portal: the Tribunal's Mercere Portal, to Harco, in a hall with an eighteen-foot statue of Tremere bearing a golden eagle on his wrist
Manufactory: makes and stores House Tremere's strategic reserve of magic and mundane goods; heavy work by enchanted tools, finishing by mundane craftsmen
Stores: caverns of arrows, rooms of swords and other war goods, kept from decay in Circle wards
Laboratories: 32, of varied specialities, with space for many more sancta; most stand idle in 1220
Treasury: over 4,000 tons of gold, and double that weight in silver, in a cavern below, nearly useless since spending much of it ruins its worth
Library: none described; its leader holds one of the twelve copies of the Book of Legacies
Defences: the gold statues of Tremere are magic items that fight for the place and attack anyone who tries to carry them off
Boon: Mystical Portal (the Mercere Portal to Harco)
Boon: Aura (Magic, up to 9 in places)
Boon: Magical Fortress (the hollowed mountain and the crown of towers)
Boon: Literate Covenfolk (Latin-speaking, numerate villagers of the old miners' stock)
Hook: House Covenant (House Tremere's manufactory and refuge)
Hook: Hermetic Services (items made to order for the House and its clients)
Tension: Albertus is a favourite target for archmage challengers
covenants.secrets:
Providing solutions: a magus pays Lycaneon to fix a setback, and the troupe must study it and design (and build or commission) the item that solves it; the problem may not be what it seems, the device may misbehave, or the client may not pay. Sample commissions: a weapon made of cabbages; swallowable items that make the carrier vomit them up later, on command, past faerie guards; a way to smuggle a stolen Gifted baby past city guards; a use for a mine that oozes custard; a weapon against demons that fear their own reflections; a better river toll than a chain.
A rapid response force: the Prima sends a team of military specialists, publicly, through the Harco network to help covenants in other Tribunals fight; between missions they rest and refit here, and the foes (faeries of many kinds, little demons that merge into big ones, fringe traditions, vast beasts, entrenched hedge wizards, corrupt magi, or raiders who claim to be Diedne) turn out to share one master.
Lycaneon was fully mobilised almost a year before the Corruption of Tytalus was announced, which suggests House Tremere knew the war was coming.

covenants.name: The Scholomance
covenants.notes:
The tower. The ground floor has the servants' and pupils' rooms, kitchens, workshops, a dining hall and Redcap guest rooms; the second, a lecture hall, small galleries and scriptoria; the third, up one always-guarded stair, the headmaster's office, the sancta, the guest rooms, the shared laboratory and the Hermetic library. Enchantments in the corridors and some rooms garble speech so it cannot be understood, and those in most study rooms blur writing for anyone but the one person touching it, so pupils cannot easily learn what others study. Neither is foolproof, but both add to the mystery.

The masters. Mature Tremere are often posted here before taking an apprentice. A magus with an apprentice at the school must teach another pupil too. Teaching is mostly one to one, or a small group when the masters are few. The school prefers magi with a taste for occult lore, natural philosophy or the liberal arts, or who hold a Supernatural Ability. One resident lately left for a distant Tribunal, so a sancta stands empty. Non-Hermetic tutors, the school's companions, teach beside them.

For players: the school explains Virtues such as Educated, Arcane Lore, Privileged Upbringing or Skilled Parens, and a saga can start with the player characters as classmates, before or just after the Opening of the Arts, with the other pupils as companions.

Founded as the Coeris mansio about 1125 (the tower was entered in 1095); the book gives no season. One of the three magi is unnamed.
covenants.summary:
The Devil's School of legend, whispered of from the Balkans to Byzantium and the Emperor's court: ten chosen students learn nature's secrets, the speech of beasts and every spell from the Devil himself for seven years, and one is never seen again. In truth it is an oppidum running a school for agents, companions and apprentices, in a squat, ivy-grown tower inside a storm regio.

Jeremiah of Tremere first broke the regio's secret and entered the tower in 1095; Coeris claimed it thirty years later as a mansio for the Redcaps of the northern Tribunal, soon trained Redcaps there, and then mundanes House Tremere had an eye on. Laniena began as part of it before moving away.

It takes ten pupils at once, for seven years: mundane scholars who heard of it through a former pupil and were invited (picked for their use to House Tremere as agents, contacts or companions; nobles, bishops and kings are rumoured among the old boys), children of the Mercere families bound to be Redcaps, who compete hard for places, and at least one Gifted youth or an apprentice whose master wanted him more broadly taught (the master then usually joins the oppidum for the class). A Gifted pupil called away is replaced, usually by a Mercere child who has followed the course since missing a place, who starts behind and has something to prove.

Teaching leans to Magic, Faerie and even Infernal Lore, rare tongues such as Arabic and Hebrew, astrology, alchemy and pharmacy; pupils with an aptitude learn Penetration and Finesse and, when a teacher is at hand, Supernatural Abilities, and even Order of Hermes Lore is taught, so the House controls what mundanes know of it. Each pupil copies texts and writes a summa or three tractatus. Old classmates often stay in touch for decades. No pupil is taken by the Devil; the legend likely comes from those who vanish into apprenticeships. Past headmasters wiped mundane pupils' memories and laid false trails, but the present policy is to make friends for the Order, so the school's ties are not advertised but not denied.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: the Furus brook at Ikafalva, a pawn of Aquam each full moon, gathered by the older Gifted pupils
School: ten pupils for seven years; magi teach a season a year in return for the library, and extend their Parma over their pupils
Library: on the second floor, mundane and occult learning and an unmatched collection on non-Hermetic magic, but nothing on the Arts or the Order
Library: on the guarded third floor, the oppidum's Hermetic texts
Laboratories: four sancta for resident magi; four guest rooms for visiting tutors, who share one large laboratory booked by the season
Stores: cellars kept fresh by enchantment; a wagon train of supplies comes once a year, with Redcaps bringing extras
Covenfolk: three soldiers only; servants who must treat every pupil as deaf and mute
Boon: Aura (Magic 5 in the regio)
Boon: Difficult Access (the tower shows only in storms)
Hook: Erratically Mobile (the tower wanders, sometimes far away)
Hook: Infamous (the Devil's School)
Tension: a papal legate lodged with the Teutonic Knights is gathering a case against it
Tension: storm wizards have twice tried to seize the tower
Tension: Simium writes to Polyaigos of the Theban Tribunal about an exchange of pupils, which old enmity blocks
covenants.secrets:
The specialist: a character with a Supernatural Ability is asked to teach it to a troubled boy; every earlier teacher of his died horribly, in ways linked to that Ability and beyond what a child could do.
A snake in the classroom: a pupil gets past the third floor's guards and vanishes with several key texts, among them a summa on the Parma Magica; he belongs to another tradition, and the school's future may hang on catching him before the book reaches his fellows.
A shadow on the mind: a former pupil dreams of dread and bloody claws, and finds that he and all his classmates have lost the same season at the school; the masters erased it for a reason.
A friend in need: an old classmate accused of a Hermetic crime in another Tribunal asks a character of standing for an alibi to buy time.
Sebastian's name echoes the dragon king Aževastjepan's; see Sebastian.

covenants.name: Coeris
covenants.notes:
The hierarchy. The Prima rules from Coeris and the Praeco (Albertus, at Lycaneon, the House's manufactory and old domus magna) serves her. Under Poena work her exarchs in the other Tribunals, her councillors, her legata and three secretaries of middle age: Horatius for operations, carrying out what the last Decennial planned, with Juturnus as his troubleshooter; Janus for contingencies, the stockpiles and odd skills the House may one day need, with Angiola; and Tatiana for emergencies and spies, with Isaac. The legata, Monica Ierne, is the House's field commander and Poena's heir: if the Prima dies or is laid low she rules until an emergency council can meet. The House chooses its Primus by appointment and duel.

Poena's way. Earlier Primi drove the House with a few striking projects, or left their councillors to themselves; Poena backs dozens of projects at once with House aid and has no single flagship that could fail and shake her rule. She sends a yearly letter to every Tremere and to the other Primi on the House's state and aims.

Rotations and Decennials. Every Tremere should spend at least a season in ten in Transylvania, and senior Tremere meet at Coeris each decade for the Decennial, bringing young magi as aides while magi of middle age keep the House's work going. Every apprentice spends time in Transylvania, including at least a season at Coeris meeting the House's leaders, and time on the frontier; two magi often take apprentices in the same year so as to swap them.

The war plans. Young Tremere are set to draw up a plan for invading a covenant of their own Tribunal, and the official plan kept at Coeris is improved by any good idea they have. The plans are named by colour: Red for taking Stonehenge and Loch Leagan, with shades such as ruby and garnet for each covenant; Blue for Normandy; White for the Alps; Black for Transylvania itself, which includes Night, a plan for taking Coeris, kept under close guard.

The Earnest Sons of the Grid and Chain. A vexillation of magi and Redcaps founded by Tremere himself, which surveys the Tribunal's wilds, sends stronger magi to tame what its scouts cannot, and proposes sites for new oppida to the Prima, who has the Praeco recruit settlers, often the apprentices of the House's allies. Its reports have grown into the Book of Places to Avoid.

The Holy Crown. Hungary's law, guarded by the Holy Crown, a living Divine being (see Hungary), lets the magi keep their own customs, laws and judges, and deal with mundanes through their servants; this is why Coeris can hold Dragonesti openly and tax it lightly, and why witchcraft, in Hungarian law, does not exist.

Founded: the book gives no year. Of the eleven unnamed magi, five are on a year's stay, two are being seasoned, and four belong to the core of thirteen.

Horror seed: magi make savants, but also nemeses, psychopaths and conspirators, and House Tremere itself is the Tribunal's largest possible conspiracy, with mystery cults, Diedne survivors and infernalists close behind. Magi conspirators strike from a distance, since the Order is good at tracing a sigil, and that only feeds the victims' paranoia.
covenants.summary:
House Tremere's seat and the place where it keeps the means to carry out its designs: the home of the Prima, who can lay hands on anything stored here the moment she judges it urgent. It is where the House's power on paper becomes strategy, and everything in its life turns, in the end, on serving a militant and ambitious House.

Dacian magicians used the site long ago, their magic surviving in remote Maramures until Tremere came, killed their faerie god, burned its heart and drank its ashes mixed with wine; its priests followed him, either converted or taking it for the right ordeal of a high priest. The Hermetic oppidum began as a place for wounded Tremere to recover, on the site of the legal covenant of Asclepius. After the Sundering the Founder, no longer trusting his domus magna where Lycaneon stands, moved his seat here and kept the name; his successor Albanus turned the anger aimed at Tremere's legacy into the glue of a House remade under him.

Some twenty magi live here, all Tremere save Archmagus Dominic of Tytalus and Isaac of Merinita. Five are here for a year, settling their apprentices or on rotation, and two are young magi being seasoned on missions while they wait for a lasting post abroad; the other thirteen are the core that makes the House's policy.
covenants.what_matters:
Seat: the Prima of House Tremere, Poena, with her secretaries and the legata
Treasury: the House's chief stores of items, vis and resources, among them the Blessings of the Dead, the talismans of Tremere who have passed
Library: the Book of Legacies (most of its twelve copies), the Book of Placements and the House's official war plans
Defences: layer on layer of wards, many by Hermanus after the Schism War, and more added after the House cast him out
Refuge: the Gate of Eurydice in the Altar of the Standards, opening on the City Below
Lands: Dragonesti, a free town on the magi's land that supplies food and craftsmen
Vis: none named in the book
Aura: none given in the book
Tension: Monica, the legata and heir, has no wish to be Prima; the succession after Poena is unsettled
Tension: House Tytalus baits the Tremere, and Dominic fears the House's patience may wear out
Tension: the previous Primus is lost in the depths of the Novgorod Tribunal, with Coeris's secrets in his memory
covenants.secrets:
The Gate of Eurydice opens on the City Below in the Magic Realm, House Tremere's last refuge (see the Gate's place).
The Night Contingency for taking Coeris is closely kept and probably salted with false information.
Janus is a lycanthrope and Tatiana a Keeper of the Silence of the Temple (see their summaries).
Poena may learn she has a wasting illness that will cloud her judgement, and quietly have possible successors weighed before a decisive certamen at the next Decennial.
Should Poena die suddenly, Monica is Prima pro tempore while the councillors are summoned, and may use the time to finish Poena's schemes and push a few of her own.
Poena plans to hold the Order's great chess competition at the Tribunal site in two years, for the House's prestige.

covenants.name: Kezdö Válasz
covenants.notes:
The forts. Besides Sarmizegethusa and Leona's Prokletije fort, two more are active, their magi left for the troupe to make. A fort can stand anywhere a story needs one, since magic raises and razes them easily; the book suggests the Bran Pass, the Madara Plateau, the Black Sea coast north of Varna, the Adriatic coast where Serbia meets the Despotate of Epirus, the Iron Gate on the Danube, the steppe beyond the Carpathians where Cuman war bands gather, and the Bulgarian-Byzantine border north of Adrianople. After each Tribunal the magi choose new sites and build a fort where none stands; a magus moves his own specialised lab, and an ordinary one is simply made anew.

Two custos envoys of the oppidum attend King Stefan of Serbia's court with the Tribunal's leave, reporting to Essedarius and Leona; their records go to Coeris.

Founded 12 August 1008 (the season given is that of the founding day). Four of its eight magi are unnamed.

Story seeds: a zmaj breaks into 'The Bones of the Founders', one of Tablinum's hidden exhibits, and the Curator calls for help, telling the magi to kill it and look at nothing; Adulio asks the characters to catch 'Golden Sunshine', a faerie horse seen on the plain of horses by the upper Danube, privately to see what trouble such a steed brings before he owns it; and the treasure of Decebalus may lie in the Vargyas River.
covenants.summary:
Less a place than a vow: its members swear to be first to meet any threat to the Tribunal and to drop their lab work and study the moment they are called. It is a chain of forts, not one site. Every member is a cives (of Coeris), foreign magi too who would otherwise be foederati, so joining is a quick road to citizenship though no sure one: Tremere keep the privilege for good, but magi of other Houses must bargain for it again if they leave.

The Tremere Norsius founded it in 1008, in the Schism War, as Primum Responsans, 'first answer', to guard the borders; it is better known by its Hungarian name. A historian more than a soldier, he took Trajan's Wall as his model: since no wall could ring the Tribunal, he built a few forts in Magic auras near the frontier, each with two magi ready to ride out while they got on with their own work. The Schism War never reached Transylvania, and the forts were never tested. His filius Gasparus spread them across the whole Tribunal as the Balkan kingdoms rose, and had each pair move to a new fort after every Tribunal meeting, every seven years, taking their sanctum markers and labs; old forts are left, reused or torn down. The leader traditionally lives in the first fort.

Four forts are active, two magi in each, with about a dozen staff per fort (men-at-arms, cooks, grooms, servants, craftsmen and an autocrat), who move the gear when the magi move; a move takes one or two seasons. Families were once barred and are now allowed. The oppidum has about 55 grogs in all, many living apart as agents in courts, towns and churches who report regularly. Each magus hands his agents rings, bracelets and charms that, when used, give him a small sign through his Parma (Essedarius's ring turns his left thumbnail blue when his agent in Niš calls), and all work on spells and devices for speaking and travelling at a distance: the oppidum owns devices that carry a magus instantly to places it holds Arcane Connections to, and members are urged to learn Rego Corpus spells that do the same. Horses are a tradition, not a necessity: Norsius made charms so horses would bear the Gifted, the leader always rides, and the younger members love the saddle.

Every 12 August, the founding day, the members meet at Sarmizegethusa for about a week to share news, introduce new members and assign them forts; with an odd number one fort holds three, its meeting room made a third lab. Magi who want to form a vexillation say so there. It is one of the easiest oppida to join, takes young Tremere and foreigners gladly, and pairs newcomers with each other or with elders; new members share its privileges and duties but must follow Essedarius, who never runs short of errands for them.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: the oppidum's stockpile at Sarmizegethusa (the book names no source)
Library: casting tablets for the ritual that raises a fort, for generic laboratories, and for one that destroys a fort (Destroy the Fort)
Enchantments: devices that carry a magus at once to places the oppidum holds Arcane Connections to, and the signal charms its agents carry
Boon: Informants (about 55 grogs, many of them agents in courts, cities and churches)
Hook: Dedicated Covenant (sworn to be first against any threat to the Tribunal)
Hook: Tribunal Border (founded to guard the frontiers)
Tension: Leona's Prokletije fort, which her sodales think a waste
Tension: Neculai's reports to Clan Sirnas on House Tremere
Tension: Adulio's eagerness for war, censured twice

covenants.name: The Zenodochia
covenants.notes:
Items. The Hippocratic Staff, of twisted hyacinth round an amber, hangs above the hall's inner lintel and gives everyone inside +9 to Recovery rolls (CrCo 34, constant). The Bowl of the Honest Traveler, a beggar's bowl on a shelf, inclines all inside to honesty (ReMe 29, no Penetration): a would-be thief must fail a Personality roll against 12 to steal. The Chest of Good Food keeps a man-month of food from spoiling (CrAn(He) 24); users should restock it. The Vermin Ward, a statue of a maimed rat, keeps out animals without Magic Resistance (ReAn 24). The Ankh of Moving Forward, of silver, heals all wounds and Wound Penalties while worn but only holds healing back: they all return when it comes off (CrCo 60, Penetration 12). An enchanted cross over the door bars demons of Might 10 or less, and an iron horseshoe bars faeries of Might 10 or less (ReVi 35 each, Penetration 12). The casting tablets hold Arms of the Salamander (regrows the latest lost limb, 6 pawns), The Rite of Healing and Universal Poultice (all wounds, and all disease, for a group, a rook of vis each).

A magus must lower his Parma to be helped, and an unconscious magus's Parma lapses at the next sunrise or sunset. The book says a season inside costs 6 Warping Points from the constant effects (a week for a Light Wound or a month for a Medium one costs 3); the Definitive Edition's Warping rules govern if they give a different count.

Finding one: a character who has not been to a nearby zenodochium rolls Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore against 9 after a year in the Tribunal or 12 for a visitor (Tremere +3), or Intelligence + Area Lore against 12; add 3 where they are rare. Few magi know where all of them are; the Tremere know most.

Story seed: the Disease Trap. Someone has swapped a zenodochium's Hippocratic Staff for an Ague Staff that gives everyone in the room the ague at every dawn (PeCo 33, a Heavy Disease Wound), its maker's sigil hidden and a Shell of False Determinations making it read as the true staff. Who laid the trap, and for whom?

The book names no Curantis for 1220. The zenodochia have no magi, aura or founding year of their own.
covenants.summary:
Not an oppidum but a service the Tribunal gives its magi: hidden safehouses where a magus taken ill or hurt on the road can find, or be carried by his grogs to, enchanted items that help him heal or heal him outright. Since they serve magi far from home, few stand near an oppidum. Most are in the countryside or the wilds (an empty wooden house by a lonely track, a cave on a quiet hillside, a hovel among the wheat), a few in the basements of town buildings, often run by a nearby oppidum's agents. Usually no one keeps them.

Each holds enchanted items, casting tablets, ordinary supplies and up to two rooks of Corpus vis. Items and tablets must stay; vis and supplies must be replaced as soon as the user can. Grogs may use them, their magus answering for any damage they do; Redcaps often lodge in them, and a message left in one is a good way to reach the Redcaps. The Tribunal wants them used and is lenient with honest mistakes: stealing vis from one is a Low Crime, though a magus who cannot repay is usually let work off the debt for the Tribunal; damaging or destroying one on purpose is a High Crime, while a magus who mends one he damaged by accident, unasked, is not prosecuted.

The Tremere generals planned the network in the Schism War, reasoning that one hidden hospital would be found and destroyed in the end, but a scatter of small ones could not all be, and that each Tremere should know only a few, in case of capture or treachery. In theory there are hundreds; many were never built, and how many stand in 1220, from a dozen to hundreds, and how keen the Tribunal still is to keep them, is the saga's choice.

The Curantis, elected at each Tribunal for the term until the next and never twice running, tours them about a season a year, repairs them, must build at least one new one in his term, and has a Quaesitor's powers in cases touching them. He draws a rich vis salary and may requisition vis from the Tribunal's stores; the elders usually agree on a single candidate before the meeting. His Notary, chosen by the previous Curantis and serving as his aedile, is a magus, often a Redcap or a magus fresh from Gauntlet.
covenants.what_matters:
Vis: up to two rooks of Corpus vis in each zenodochium, to be replaced after use
Enchantments: the Hippocratic Staff, the Bowl of the Honest Traveler, the Chest of Good Food, the Vermin Ward, the Ankh of Moving Forward, and the two wards against disease demons and faeries
Library: casting tablets of Arms of the Salamander, The Rite of Healing and Universal Poultice in each
Hook: Zenodochium (the Minor Hook a covenant takes for one within a day's travel; visited by the Curantis every few years)
Tension: the Bran Pass zenodochium is held by rebel knights
Tension: the Zadar zenodochium and its surgeon are lost

covenants.name: Leviathan
covenants.notes: The book gives no founding year, aura or season.
covenants.summary:
House Tremere's mothballed naval base on the Adriatic, so named in its war plans, to be woken in wartime if Shrouded Bay looks unsafe. The Tremere and the Mercere each run a small trading fleet on the Adriatic, the safer of the Tribunal's two coasts and one of the world's busiest seas.

No magus lives there. Phillip of Lycaneon holds an Arcane Connection to it and would likely move there in a naval war; with his skill at making ships' parts and the base's facilities, the House would lack crews, not hulls.
covenants.what_matters:
Facilities: stores and works to fit out ships, for Phillip's craft
Hook: Superiors (House Tremere's war plans)

tribunals.name: The Transylvanian Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The Tribunal of the Carpathian Basin: the Great Plain of Hungary and the mountains that ring it (the Alps excepted), with lands to the west and south that carry it to the shores of the Adriatic and the Black Sea. Its southern edge follows no river or ridge, only the vis sources the magi on either side have claimed. Werewolves, vampires and dragons haunt its forests and passes, and folk magicians hunt them with silver, prayer and hawthorn; yet mundane society here favours the magi more than anywhere in the West. Hungarian law lets them keep their own Code and courts, nobles owe no fealty for their land, and magic is no crime, so the Order rules what it owns openly.

It is House Tremere's Tribunal, and the House's proof that magi who work together can build a better world, patiently and over generations. The Prima of Tremere, Poena, at Coeris, makes the policy that governs Transylvania; the Tremere vote as a block, so they get what they want lawfully and by vote, and they want the Tribunal as an institution to thrive. The magi owe far more to the whole than Western magi do, and live in a single economy of specialised settlements rather than self-sufficient manors.

Oppida and the five legal covenants. Magi live in oppida, camps independent of one another, whose members come and go as their projects and the House's needs change. A Transylvanian covenant is something else: one of the five legal bodies a Grand Tribunal left the Tribunal after the Sundering, which the Tremere turned into classes of citizenship. Each magus holds a privilege, a written agreement with the Praeco witnessed by a Quaesitor and read into the Peripheral Code: cives (of Coeris), socii (of Domostron), coloniae (of Asclepius), hospites (of Diodorus) or foederati (of Pannonia). One oppidum mixes magi of several privileges by rule, and each has one or two aediles, the odd members who guard against corruption.

The officers. The Praeco, Archmagus Albertus of Lycaneon, leads the Tribunal in name, chosen by vote but only with the Prima's approval, and keeps the office only while he keeps her favour; he levies the taxes the Tribunal approves, pays the Redcaps' and Quaesitores' stipends, and issues promissory notes. Benilda of Seuthopolis, the senior Quaesitor and legal head of Domostron, presides at the meetings, witnesses privileges and hears accusations. Other offices: the aediles of each oppidum, the Curantis of the zenodochia with his Notary, the Curator of Tablinum, and the lictors.

The meeting. The Tribunal meets every seven years in a regio at the Shipka Pass, near Seuthopolis, which House Guernicus keeps for the Praeco. The book gives no year for the next meeting, so 1221 is assumed, and no season, so summer is assumed. The great meetings are short and seek consensus, mostly reading what has already been agreed into the Code; the magi come for the company and the deals made around them. Criminal cases go to the emergency Tribunals the Quaesitores call there every year, where Tremere advocates cast the proxies of all their Transylvanian housemates.

About 82 magi live in the Tribunal's ten oppida: Coeris, Laniena, Evredika, Seuthopolis, Tablinum, Old Histria and Shrouded Bay, Lycaneon, the Scholomance and Kezdö Válasz. The zenodochia, its roadside hospitals for magi, and Leviathan, a naval cache kept for war, belong to the Tribunal; Gigas, across the border, is a Theban covenant the Tremere use as their cat's paw.

Questions for 1221: the Valley of the Thracian Kings, which Benilda is keeping closed against the Tremere necromancers; a Mercere Portal from Old Histria to Venice; the standing of the Tribunal's own Redcaps with Harco; whether Laniena's training of Fectores is lawful; raids on Evredika's vis that point at Gigas; and a papal legate lodged with the Teutonic Knights, asking about the Scholomance.

Stories. The Dragon War is the saga's great frame: the Pax Draconis hangs on a dragon unseen for fifty years, and any spark could set the Tribunal's dragons on each other and on men. Others wait for the storyguide to begin them: the Teutonic Knights' fall in 1222 and 1225, the Mongols, the Bosnian crusade, the Valley of the Thracian Kings, the return of Zalmoxis, the Székely taltós, Poena's succession and the papal legate hunting the Scholomance. The Tribunal also suits horror: monster against savant, the psychopath, the horde, the conspiracy, the madness of the frontier, the changing body, nature's revenge and the cycle that repeats; the seeds sit on the places they use.
tribunals.history:
Dacians, Romans and dragons. The Getae, the first tribe of the region named in history, were conquered by Darius of Persia. Their god Zalmoxis, said by his cult to have studied magic with Pythagoras on Samos, was once worshipped openly and now only in the hidden places of the Carpathians. Rome made the land Dacia; Trajan bridged the Danube and Decebalus's treasure is still lost. In the second century Fetillusclaviceps, the Roman dragon, forged the Pax Draconis: dragons would not war together, would keep their violence at home, would defer to the stronger and leave men be, and a wife taken without a greater dragon's leave made the taker an outlaw. Goths, Huns, Gepids and Avars drove the Vlachs into the hills; the Goths beat Valens near Adrianople in 376, and the Huns sacked Nikopolis in 447.

Slavs, Bulgars and Magyars. The Slavs crossed the Carpathians in the sixth and seventh centuries, led, their tales say, by a taltós hermit of matchless power, and the Seven Tribes ruled the Balkans for about a century. Khan Asparukh's Bulgars crossed the Danube between 679 and 681 to found the First Bulgarian Empire. More than a thousand years ago the taltós, wise men of the Huns, turned their vampire-slaying magic on one another and all but wiped themselves out within a few years. The Szeklers claim descent from Attila's rearguard and allied with the Magyars when they came; Saint Stephen made Hungary Christian, gave it to the Virgin and first taught the doctrine of the living Holy Crown. In the eleventh century Pechenegs, Magyars and Uzes overran Bulgaria in turn, and the Cumans took the lands east of the Carpathians.

The Founder and the legal covenants. Dacian magicians held the site of Coeris in Maramures, beyond the reach of Rome and the Church, until Tremere killed their faerie god, burned its heart and swallowed its ashes in wine; its priests became his followers, and Coeris was first built as a refuge for wounded Tremere. He chose Lycaneon for its metals and mined its gold out in the covenant's first decades. Asclepius began as a settlement of Dacian sorcerers on the site of Coeris, long since absorbed by the House; Domostron was founded by Tremere's Hermetic allies, and Theban raiders destroyed its first site; Diodorus housed the followers of the faerie magician Muj, now a small sect of House Tremere; Pannonia was a fortified Tremere covenant on the border of three Tribunals, until a great monastery at the springs of its river killed its aura and its magi became the first to scatter into oppida. Centuries ago Pannonia sold nearly all its concessions to the chief Mercere of the Tribunal.

Refugees, war and watchfulness. Covenants worn down by quarrels in neighbouring Tribunals have sought refuge here as foederati of Pannonia: the Covenant of the Four Divinities, Verditius magi of the Cabeiri cult, came from the Theban Tribunal and became Seuthopolis, long since the seat of the Quaesitors and hoplites; Histria came from the Roman Tribunal, with its chapter house at Shrouded Bay on Cres, first built to guard Cres against Transylvanian Tremere. After the Schism War Lycaneon was enlarged and fully manned for decades, Hermanus raised many of Coeris's defences until his obsession had him cast out, and the House compiled the Diedne sigils now kept at Seuthopolis. Some storm wizards joined House Ex Miscellanea in that war and fought beside the Tremere. Lycaneon was fully mobilised almost a year before the Corruption of Tytalus was disclosed at Tribunal, and Tasgilla, the corrupted Prima of Tytalus, had spread infernal taint through spells and texts. A few decades ago one Primus had the Redcaps seek Gifted Arab and African children for his House to raise.

cases.title: The Valley of the Thracian Kings
cases.brought_by: House Tremere's necromancers, with House Verditius
cases.charge: Four years ago a Tremere necromancer serving as a hoplite found the burial ground of the ancient Thracian kings, close to Seuthopolis. The Tremere necromancers want it opened, and the Verditius too, for the Thracians honoured smith gods. Benilda, wary of necromancers in good spirits, bars the site; she knows the Tremere will win in the end and hopes to look first or to shape who digs and why.

cases.title: Harco and the Tribunal's Redcaps
cases.charge: The Tremere want the Tribunal's true Redcaps increased by 35, which Harco, with only 150 members in the whole House, sees as upsetting its balance. For now Harco accepts the heads of the Transylvanian Redcap families as members and their kin as close agents, whom the Tribunal calls Redcaps anyway; the truce may fail if the Roman side presses for control, and a new one needs brokering. Senior local Redcaps also want Volante to raise heirs rather than take a new Gifted leader from Harco each generation.

cases.title: A Portal from Old Histria to Venice
cases.charge: Magi have long talked of a Mercere Portal joining Old Histria to its chapter house in Venice, in the Roman Tribunal. If the Tribunal decides on it, the Praeco must carry it out: a special levy of vis, Redcaps guarding it on the road, a colona who cannot pay, promissory notes and envoys to Harco, where Old Histria's chief Redcap must argue for it, and the invested arch brought back from Harco.

cases.title: Whether Laniena is lawful
cases.brought_by: (not yet brought: magi who think it so)
cases.charge: Some magi hold that raising Gifted children as Fectores, denied Hermetic magic, makes their masters delinquent and deprives them of their magical power, a High Crime. Laniena answers that the trainees are not members of the Order, so the Code does not protect them, and that each is offered the Order's protection once trained. Tremere policy backs Laniena for now, but the charge waits for the day the House is displeased.

cases.title: Murat of Terezin's secret
cases.against: Murat the Younger of Ex Miscellanea (Laniena)
cases.charge:
Secret; a case can be brought only once someone finds out.

Secrets
Murat of Terezin, founder of the Fectores, was secretly a dhampir and rose as a vampire after his death; he now lives as a kukudhi far from Laniena with his fourth mortal wife, father of more than twenty dhampir children. Only his pupil Murat the Younger knows, and has let him be. If Lexander learns of it, House Tremere's anger could fall on the whole oppidum.

cases.title: Gigas and Evredika's vis
cases.against: Gigas (Theban Tribunal), or whoever is framing it
cases.charge: A hunting party led by a nobleman with a pet white wolf has stripped every one of Evredika's vis sources. Gigas, House Tremere's thinly hidden cat's paw in the Theban Tribunal, was told to leave Evredika's claims alone and seems the likeliest thief; if its denials are honest, someone is setting it up, and the question is who and why. A matter between two Tribunals.

cases.title: The papal legate and the Scholomance
cases.against: A papal legate lodged with the Teutonic Knights
cases.charge: Legends of the Devil's School have reached Rome, and a legate has come to look into the Scholomance and its supposed diabolism, staying with the Teutonic Order while he builds his case. So far he has only hearsay, since only magi and former pupils know anything real; the Tribunal must decide how to keep it so without breaking the Code.

rulings.title: The five legal covenants
rulings.says: After the Sundering a Grand Tribunal capped the Tribunal at five named covenants: Coeris, Domostron, Asclepius, Diodorus and Pannonia. All five have since moved or changed how they admit members, but in law they still stand, and no new covenant can be added. A body of outsiders that joins the Tribunal enters Pannonia. The Tremere do not ask for the limit to be lifted, lest it stir old fears, and no one else gains by asking.

rulings.title: Privileges
rulings.says: Every resident magus holds a privilege: a written agreement with the Praeco, on the Tribunal's behalf, that sets the magus's place in Transylvanian society. A Quaesitor witnesses it and it is read into the Peripheral Code at a meeting. There are five broad kinds, one for each legal covenant, but each is bargained for, and terms may be added later as reward or punishment. A magus may leave the Tribunal freely, returning what he was paid for unfinished work; one who goes with great items, much vis or other treasures is pursued by the Tremere.

rulings.title: Cives (Coeris)
rulings.says: Every Tremere belongs to Coeris, and may resign and rejoin at will. Other magi may be made cives as a mark of the Tribunal's esteem. A cives may draw on House Tremere's aid, send a Tremere proxy to the House's Decennial, stand for any office including Praeco, raise apprentices, move between oppida (if not Tremere), and wear black or grey at meetings; where cives are the larger group of an oppidum they choose its aedile from the others. In return a cives must live as the Tremere admire: cooperate, work usefully, muster for war and pay taxes.

rulings.title: Socii (Domostron)
rulings.says: The socii are allies of other Houses treated much as if they were Tremere: nearly all the Quaesitores, Redcaps and dedicated hoplites, who are socii unless they are cives. They may hold any office but Praeco, raise an apprentice, draw dedicated resources and crisis taxes for their work, and wear designs like Decorations; where they are the larger group they name three candidates for aedile and the Praeco picks one. They must do their duty or renegotiate, give no one a fair cause for Wizard's War (as the Praeco judges), ask leave to found an oppidum, stand in as aediles when none can be found, and wear their badges at meetings.

rulings.title: Coloniae (Asclepius)
rulings.says: The coloniae are young magi from other Tribunals settled under close terms to open up neglected corners of the land. They are promised aid in war or disaster, the resources named in their privilege and a share of new ones found. They may not choose their aedile, seek any office but aedile, call themselves archmagi, take apprentices without leave, invite other magi in (save Quaesitores, Redcaps and hoplites), behave scandalously, or wear what looks like a Decoration they have not earned. At meetings they go unshod (sandals and slippers are now allowed) and may eat no aphrodisiac, from shellfish and truffles to carrots and pepper.

rulings.title: Hospites (Diodorus)
rulings.says: The hospites, the Tribunal's guests, are magi hired to practise a skill for House Tremere, and most live at Lycaneon. They are paid fairly, use what their task is given, escape many taxes, are protected if War is declared on them, and are not called to Wizard's Marches. They must ask leave before seeking office, taking an apprentice, binding a familiar, making a talisman, founding or changing oppidum, voting for a particular aedile, or wearing what looks like a Decoration; a privilege may grant some of these in advance, for less pay.

rulings.title: Foederati (Pannonia)
rulings.says: The foederati are magi of covenants that left neighbouring Tribunals for shelter here, and each keeps the customs written into its privilege, offensive to the Tremere or not, so long as it breaks neither the Code nor the Tribunal's peace. They keep the resources they held when they joined, train apprentices (the eldest is taken on as a foederatus too), move oppidum with notice and may stand for any office. They need leave to drop the duties their privilege names, which only the Praeco and the magus together can change, to use the title archmagus, found oppida, invite magi in, or trade vis or items with outsiders other than the socii. Should Pannonia ever lack outsiders, some magi of other covenants join it automatically, so it never lapses.

rulings.title: The leaders of the legal covenants
rulings.says: To keep the Tribunal whole after the Sundering, Tremere granted concessions to the other covenants' leaders, now paid by the Tribunal. Asclepius's members elect a leader each year, who is invited to Coeris for the Triumph of Asclepius: sixteen pawns of vis, three pounds of pure gold, six books of his choosing copied from a certain library, a fine dinner and lesser tokens, in return for minor duties to the other leaders that take about two seasons. Magi of any covenant, and non-residents, may hold it. The hospites elect their leader every seven years, with the Praeco's approval, for a smaller yearly payment. Domostron is led by the senior Quaesitor and Pannonia by the Orphic cult of the south, whose members long ago sold their concessions to the chief Mercere.

rulings.title: Oppida
rulings.says: Every magus must belong to an oppidum in some sense, and keep broadly aware of what its other members are doing. An oppidum must have at least two members, at least one of them cives, and may not be made up wholly of one House, so in practice each has a Tremere and someone who is not.

rulings.title: Aediles
rulings.says: Each oppidum has an aedile, the odd member set there to keep House Tremere from corruption and the others from treason; where cives and non-cives are equal in number it has two. Aediles have no set duties, but may demand an urgent audience with the Praeco and the chief Quaesitor, and the Quaesitores treat an aedile's disappearance, or War declared on one, gravely.

rulings.title: Decorations
rulings.says: The Tribunal honours service with five crowns, worn as jewellery or embroidery on a magus's robes, never awarded twice to the same magus; a higher one replaces a lower. The Laurel goes to the magus who leads a campaign against a foe that could destroy the Order (no one now wears it); the Myrtle to the general of a lesser campaign of more than one magical battle; the Oak to one who plans such a campaign without fighting in it; the Grass to a magus who saves other magi from death, first given to the defenders of covenants against the Diedne; and the Parsley for the killing blow on a magus the Tribunal has cast out.

rulings.title: The Praeco
rulings.says: The Praeco is chosen by vote, not by age, and needs the Prima of Tremere's approval to take office and her goodwill to keep it. He has wider powers than Praecones elsewhere, ceded by the House slowly and reversibly. The Praeco appoints the Tribunal's envoys and asks magi to settle when the Prima wants an oppidum founded.

rulings.title: Taxes and stipends
rulings.says: The Praeco gathers taxes for the projects each meeting assigns him, and the cives, socii, coloniae and some foederati must give reasonable aid to them. A large vis source is reserved for his use, once meant for the upkeep of the meeting site's wards, which the Quaesitores now see to. He also collects the stipends the Peripheral Code sets for the Redcaps and Quaesitores, and his Redcaps deliver them, so the Tremere can see what is claimed without spying and no one can call it a bribe from the House.

rulings.title: Promissory notes
rulings.says: Before he could tax, the Praeco borrowed against his reserved vis by issuing notes promising payment, and he still issues them for trade and diplomacy. Old notes never redeemed pass from hand to hand as a currency of great value. Forging one is a crime, held to be fraud aimed at robbing a magus of the vis that is his power.

rulings.title: Annual emergency Tribunals
rulings.says: Elsewhere the Quaesitores call emergency Tribunals when they must; in Transylvania House Guernicus calls one every year at the Tribunal site, to give swifter justice and accept newly trained apprentices sooner. A group of Tremere advocates holds proxies for every Transylvanian Tremere, so the vote always suits the House, which uses these meetings to keep its allies content and often concedes more than the votes require.

rulings.title: Wizard's War
rulings.says: Magi keep their right under the Code to declare War, but the Tribunal strongly prefers that wizards fight wizards only in Marches voted at an emergency Tribunal. Quarrels go first to mediation by the Quaesitores or the Prima's people, and then to certamen; private Wars are very rare.

rulings.title: Certamen in place of War
rulings.says: A challenge to certamen says the challenger would kill his rival if he were less civilised. The winner is treated as having spared a life he could have taken, the loser lives by his mercy, and the winner has the right to strike the loser once in the face. Certamen rules are otherwise the Definitive Edition's.

rulings.title: Certamen for love
rulings.says: Most duels are fought for love, as sport or over small matters.
