Before two witnesses the Tribunal could question, the duellists declare that it is for love, the stake, how it is won if not by yielding (first sound blow, first wound or unconsciousness are common), forgiveness in advance for any hurt, and that the loser yields. They may not strike a blow at the end, use vis, gamble basely, wager an officer's duties, duel naked or drunk, use spells or items (or let onlookers) to sway the result, couple during the duel, or challenge one worn down by an earlier duel.

rulings.title: Dealings with outsiders
rulings.says: Many oppida may not make treaties with foreign covenants or Tribunals. Trading arrangements with outsiders need either a place in the Peripheral Code or the Praeco's approval, witnessed by a Quaesitor; the Praeco's appointees speak for the Tribunal abroad.

rulings.title: Settlers and Gifted children
rulings.says: No magus may bring a Gifted child into the Tribunal or invite a magus to settle. He may instead ask the Praeco to do it, which lets the Tremere govern how many magi live here.

rulings.title: Sales of vis and enchanted items
rulings.says: Only the Praeco, the Prima of Tremere, the socii and their agents may sell vis or enchanted items to outsiders. Old Histria is the registry for every such sale in the Tribunal; the goods need not go there, as matching letters notarised by a Quaesitor suffice. The Praeco's people may bid for anything of interest, and buyers of common vis may consult the list of notes kept by the master of the vis trade at Old Histria.

rulings.title: Magical animals
rulings.says: Magical animals may not be exported without licence, which lets House Tremere, ever seeking breeding stock for war, buy first on exports and bid alongside on imports. Selling through the Redcaps is lawful but recorded.

rulings.title: One name to a Tremere
rulings.says: No two Tremere magi in the Tribunal may share a name, so that the House's records can tell each apart; a maga who arrives bearing a name already held may have to defend it by certamen.

rulings.title: Amaranth
rulings.says: Amaranth, a faerie flower whose vis gives magi pleasant visions, addiction and Warping, is destroyed wherever it is found in Transylvania.

rulings.title: Lictors
rulings.says: Lictors, magi sworn to long service as hoplites, guard the Quaesitores and follow their orders. They may call on any cives, socius, foederatus or colonus for reasonable aid, the Tribunal judging afterwards what was reasonable for the danger. All belong to one legal covenant and so wear the same red and silver sash, pinned with a winged silver brooch, the astraea, each with its own variation. Carrying a copy of a lictor's badge is a serious crime.

rulings.title: The zenodochia
rulings.says: The Tribunal keeps safehouses for sick or wounded magi along its roads, and wants them used. Taking vis from one is a Low Crime, though a magus who cannot repay is usually let work off the debt for the Tribunal; damaging or destroying one on purpose is a High Crime, while one who repairs accidental damage unasked is not prosecuted. Items and casting tablets must stay; vis and supplies used must be replaced.

rulings.title: The Curantis
rulings.says: Each meeting elects a Curantis to serve until the next, usually the single candidate the elders agree on beforehand; no one may serve two terms running. He tours the zenodochia for about a season a year, repairs them, must build at least one new one in his term, and has a Quaesitor's powers in cases touching them. He is paid generously in vis and may draw on the Tribunal's stores. His Notary, chosen by the previous Curantis and often a Redcap, serves as his aedile.

rulings.title: The Curator of Tablinum
rulings.says: The Curator, who keeps the museum oppidum of Tablinum, holds office for life. The Transylvania Chronicle kept there is the authoritative record of the Tribunal's history and its rulings.

rulings.title: Mercere votes
rulings.says: By the terms of their covenant with the Tribunal, only Gifted Mercere vote at its meetings; in exchange the Tribunal lets the families of unGifted Redcaps grow as large as they like.

rulings.title: Hedge wizards and Laniena
rulings.says: The Code's Join or Die provision applies to Gifted hedge wizards. The Tribunal's policy lets Laniena train Gifted children as Fectores, hunters who are not Hermetic magi, on the ground that trainees are outside the Order and so outside the Code; once trained, each is offered the Order's protection. Laniena knows it lasts only on sufferance, since the High Crime of depriving a magus of his magic could be charged whenever the Tremere wished.

diary.title: The Order of Hermes founded
diary.details: The Order is founded. The Transylvania Chronicle, kept in Tablinum's exhibit hall, begins its record with this year, though sceptics note how little it says of House Tremere's beginnings.

diary.title: A skirmish at the Shipka Pass
diary.details: In the Order's first years the Founder Tremere fights a band of Theban magi at the Shipka Pass, the best road through Bulgaria's mountains. A regio lies beside the battlefield: some say Tremere knew of it and laid his ambush from it, others that a Twilight born of the fight's strain made it. For long afterwards House Tremere and the Theban covenants meet there to reflect and to sign their treaties. (The book gives no year.)

diary.title: Krum takes Hungary and Transylvania
diary.details: Khan Krum the Conqueror adds the lands of Hungary and Transylvania to the First Bulgarian Empire.

diary.title: Tremere wears the Roman dragon's face
diary.details: Early in the ninth century, when dragon raids flare up in defiance of the Pax Draconis, the Founder Tremere takes the shape of Fetillusclaviceps, the Roman dragon who made the peace, and puts down the rebels. He never speaks of it, and whatever record of his reasons existed was lost in the Sundering. (The book gives no exact year.)

diary.title: Death of Krum
diary.details: Krum, who had beaten two Byzantine emperors in battle and laid siege to Constantinople, dies suddenly, and no one knows quite how.

diary.title: The Sundering
diary.details: Tremere's bid to master the Order ends in the Sundering. No longer trusting his domus magna at what is now Lycaneon, he moves his seat, and its name, to Coeris in Maramures, where the Covenant of Asclepius then stood; Lycaneon stays the House's manufactory. His successor Albanus turns the Order's anger at Tremere's memory into a means of binding the House together. A Grand Tribunal caps the Tribunal at five named covenants, Coeris, Domostron, Asclepius, Diodorus and Pannonia, which still exist in law though every one has since moved or changed its membership. To keep the others from seceding, Tremere grants concessions to their leaders, and the covenants bind one another by contract; the Triumph of Asclepius is still paid from them.

diary.title: Akilina finds Tablinum's site
diary.details: The maga Akilina comes upon a place in the Danube delta where many regiones lie one over another, the future site of Tablinum. (The book says only the middle of the ninth century.)

diary.title: Tablinum founded
diary.details: In the years after the Sundering Tablinum is founded as a storehouse for artifacts, with Akilina its first Curator. Since the Tribunal may hold only five covenants, it has no official standing and no recognised residents until the custom of oppida spreads, when it remakes itself as an oppidum with Curators who live there. Its founders are said to have walked a ritual path through the regiones, fixing an Arcane Connection to each level and destroying the path behind them.

diary.title: Cyril and Methodius's church in Bulgaria
diary.details: Boris I, the first Christian khan of Bulgaria, baptised Michael, welcomes the mission of Saints Cyril and Methodius, from which the Bulgarian Church takes its descent.

diary.title: Potitus opens Tablinum
diary.details: Akilina names her apprentice Potitus her successor and resigns. The first Curator to make his home at Tablinum, he opens what had been a closed storehouse to study. By this year the Chronicle already mentions its regiones and the Arcane Connections that reach them.

diary.title: Akilina vanishes
diary.details: Tablinum's first Curator disappears and is presumed dead.

diary.title: Symeon's Bulgarian Church
diary.details: Symeon, son of Boris and the first Bulgarian ruler to style himself tsar rather than khan, makes the Bulgarian Church autonomous. By the peace of 927 the patriarch of Constantinople accepts its independence, and it soon has a patriarch of its own.

diary.title: Tiberia shares the Curatorship; Saint Ivan of Rila dies
diary.details: Potitus appoints Tiberia, a Tremere general, as his successor, and for a short time the two share the office; Potitus's term ends in 948. In the same year the hermit, healer and mystic Ivan Rilski dies; his body, still uncorrupted, now lies at Tarnovo, and he is Bulgaria's patron saint.

diary.title: Evredika instituted
diary.details: The Cult of Orpheus had worshipped in the Rhodope mountains for decades as an informal cult, and when it joined the Order its sacred sites there became Hermetic ground. In this year Evredika, named for Eurydice in the Bulgarian tongue, becomes a formal oppidum.

diary.title: The zenodochia devised
diary.details: During the Schism War the Tremere generals plan a network of tiny hidden hospitals, the zenodochia, reasoning that one hospital oppidum would be found and destroyed in time, while a web of small ones could not be, and that no single captured magus would know more than a few of them. Hundreds are planned; many are never built. (The book gives no year.)

diary.title: Tiberia falls; Anatolus Curator
diary.details: Tiberia is killed in the Schism War. Anatolus, also a Tremere general, succeeds her, the first Curator of Tablinum chosen by the Tribunal rather than by the one before. He becomes known for strange battle magic, said to come from Tablinum's halls.

diary.title: Kezdö Válasz founded
diary.details: Norsius of House Tremere, more scholar than soldier, founds Primum Responsans, better known by its Hungarian name Kezdö Válasz, to guard the Tribunal's borders in the Schism War. Taking Trajan's Wall as his model, he builds a few forts in magic auras near the frontier, each with two magi who study between alarms; his own first fort stands in the ruins of Sarmizegethusa, Decebalus's palace. The war never reaches Transylvania, and the forts are never tested. Later his filius Gasparus spreads the forts across the whole Tribunal and has each pair of magi move to a new one after every Tribunal meeting.

diary.title: Bulgaria falls to Byzantium; Anatolus slain
diary.details: The First Bulgarian Empire, founded by Asparukh's Bulgars, falls to Byzantine rule. The Bulgarian Church loses its independence, is reduced to an archbishopric at Ohrid and filled with Greek clergy. In the same year the Curator Anatolus dies in a Wizard's War, and Tablinum has no Curator for two years.

diary.title: Silus Curator
diary.details: Silus becomes Curator of Tablinum.

diary.title: Silus Marched; Justius Curator
diary.details: Silus is accused of infernalism and Marched. His successor Justius is said to have taken apart a number of infernal exhibits and driven demons out of many of Tablinum's regio levels during his long tenure.

diary.title: Scribonius Curator
diary.details: Scribonius becomes Curator of Tablinum and writes the first catalogue of its exhibits to claim completeness.

diary.title: Croatia offered to Hungary
diary.details: The Trpimirović line of Croatian kings ends in a feeble quarrel between brothers, and the nobles of the north invite Ladislaus I of Hungary to rule. Croatia has been a vassal principality of Hungary ever since.

diary.title: Villages bound to their churches
diary.details: A Church council in Hungary rules that a village with a church may not move far from it, beginning the end of the Magyars' wandering villages.

diary.title: Jeremiah enters the ghostly castle
diary.details: The Order had long known of a phantom castle in the Carpathians; this year Jeremiah of Tremere solves the secret of its regio and becomes the first magus to enter the tower. One inhabitant waits there, and he has not aged since.

diary.title: Coloman's law: witches do not exist
diary.details: King Coloman the Learned of Hungary decrees that, as witches do not exist, no one may be tried for witchcraft. The Quaesitors look into it as discreetly as they can but find no magus behind it, and the law still stands. (The book says only the eleventh century; Coloman reigned from 1095 to 1116.)

diary.title: Scribonius leaves; Calpurnius Curator
diary.details: Scribonius resigns as Curator, quits House Tremere and joins House Jerbiton in the Theban Tribunal. His successor Calpurnius greatly enlarges Tablinum's Faerie collection.

diary.title: Murat and Radomir purge the vampires; Laniena founded
diary.details:
The vampire of a dead magus hunts out dhampirs, has them trained and then kills them to make more vampires, the latest of the infiltrations that have dogged House Tremere. The famed hunter Murat of Terezin comes to Coeris and with the young Radomir of Tremere clears every vampire from the House; Murat kills the nest's master himself. The two ask the Tribunal for an oppidum to train hunters, and once Murat joins House Ex Miscellanea the Praeco agrees. Working from old initiation scripts a Gnostic scholar took down while spying on a taltós clan, they learn after years of trials to Open the Gifted to the Hunters' Arts; Radomir calls them interfectores, soon shortened to Fectores. Laniena begins as part of the Scholomance and later moves to the Aggtelek caves. House Tremere now forbids its magi to take a dhampir as apprentice. (The book says about a hundred years ago.)

Secrets
Murat of Terezin was himself a dhampir, and became a vampire when he died. He survives as a kukudhi, a vampire passing as a man, living far from Laniena with his fourth mortal wife and fathering dhampirs. Only Murat the Younger knows, and lets him be for the hunters his children give Laniena.

diary.title: Coeris takes the Scholomance
diary.details: Thirty years after Jeremiah's entry Coeris claims the ghostly tower and makes it a mansio for the Redcaps of the Tribunal's north. Within a few years it is training Redcaps, and soon after mundanes of use to House Tremere.

diary.title: Akilina seen again; Scribonius dies
diary.details: Magi studying at Tablinum report meeting Akilina, or someone who claims to be her, in the maze of its regiones, two centuries after she vanished. Scribonius, the former Curator, dies this year.

diary.title: Stefan Nemanja serves the emperor
diary.details: Stefan Nemanja, a Serbian prince of modest beginnings and then a Byzantine vassal, helps the emperor in his war on Hungary.

diary.title: The Roman dragon's last sighting
diary.details:
Fetillusclaviceps, keeper of the Pax Draconis, is seen for the last time. He had shown himself only half a dozen times in three centuries, never to a magus, and his lair has never been found. (The book says only more than fifty years before 1220.)

Secrets
Some Tremere wonder whether the later sightings were the dragon at all, or magi of their own House repeating the Founder's disguise.

diary.title: Pantino
diary.details: Stefan Nemanja turns on his Byzantine overlord and beats an imperial army at the Battle of Pantino.

diary.title: Nestor Curator
diary.details: Nestor succeeds Calpurnius as Curator of Tablinum, an office held for life, and becomes known for his research into regiones.

diary.title: Nemanja taken to Constantinople
diary.details: Nemanja allies with Venice, Hungary and German princes to throw off Byzantine rule, but Serbian feuds, a Venetian mutiny and plague wreck the campaign. Manuel Komnenos invades Raška, besieges Ras and carries Nemanja to Constantinople in chains; against all expectation the two become friends, and Nemanja returns as the emperor's strategos and the sole lawful ruler of the Serbs.

diary.title: The Asen brothers free Bulgaria
diary.details: Three brothers, Teodor Petar, Ivan Asen and Kaloyan, lead the Bulgarians out of Byzantine rule and found the Second Bulgarian Empire. Their origins are a mystery, perhaps Bulgarian, perhaps Vlach or Cuman, and their inherited gift for swaying crowds troubles the Order. Cuman tribes shelter the rebel princes after their first army is beaten and supply the core of the next.

diary.title: The Teutonic Order founded at Acre
diary.details: Barbarossa died in 1189 and most of his German nobles went home, but a faithful few stay for the siege of Acre. Ill and neglected by the French and English Hospitallers, crusaders from Bremen and Lübeck found a hospital order for Germans, backed by Duke Friedrich of Swabia, and Pope Celestine III approves it. (The book says some twenty years before 1220.)

diary.title: Nemanja abdicates
diary.details: Stefan Nemanja retires and hands Serbia to his second son, Stefan, passing over the eldest, Vukan.

diary.title: Kaloyan tsar
diary.details: Kaloyan begins his reign and restores the Bulgarian Empire; his Cuman bride seals an alliance with the nomads that must be renewed by rite each summer. New German crusaders reach the Holy Land and find the Teutonic hospital flourishing.

diary.title: The Teutonic Knights take up the sword
diary.details: Seeing the crusader kingdom's border forts badly manned, the newcomers decide the Teutonic brothers, former knights, can fight as well as nurse, and the pope gives the Order a new charter as a military order.

diary.title: Death of Stefan Nemanja
diary.details: Nemanja dies, and holy oil begins to flow from his tomb, so the people call him the Myrrh-flowing.

diary.title: Saint Simeon; Eudocia driven out
diary.details: Less than a year after his death the Eastern Church canonises Stefan Nemanja. Stefan II accuses his first wife, Eudocia Angelina, daughter of Emperor Alexios Angelos and mother of five of his children, of adultery and drives her from Serbia. About this time Hungary stops exporting slaves, probably as part of the king's plan to people the kingdom's edges.

diary.title: Zadar sacked
diary.details: Crusaders raid and destroy Zadar, Croatia's richest port and a possession of the King of Hungary, and little is done to dislodge the Venetians.

diary.title: Tarnovo's primate; the Zadar zenodochium
diary.details: Pope Innocent III names the Archbishop of Tarnovo primate of all Bulgaria and Wallachia, tying the Asens' church to Rome, though Ohrid stays Orthodox. Soon after the violence at Zadar, House Tremere builds a zenodochium in a regio within a magical lacuna in the city and staffs it with a skilled surgeon and his assistants. Some months later the House loses touch with them, and the regio itself seems to vanish.

diary.title: Constantinople falls; Adulio joins Kezdö Válasz
diary.details: Constantinople falls to the Latins, and the Latin Church soon controls much of the city; the magi of Thebes learn what crusading armies can do. Two months later Adulio of House Tremere, just out of his apprenticeship, joins Kezdö Válasz to keep the same fate from Transylvania. In Serbia Vukan's resentment breaks into civil war against his brother Stefan II, who wins but cannot take any of the lost Byzantine lands. A loyal Croatian noble wrests Zadar back from the crusaders.

diary.title: Baldwin captured; Venice takes the coast
diary.details: Tsar Kaloyan captures Emperor Baldwin of the Latin Empire, who is held in the tower above Tarnovo's Frankish quarter that still bears his name. Venice takes Dubrovnik, which pays it tribute and harbours its galleys, and regains Zadar, this time by a treaty that makes the Venetians overseers rather than occupiers; the townsfolk see through it.

diary.title: Saint Simeon comes to Studenica
diary.details: Nemanja's relics are carried from Mount Athos to the monastery of Studenica.

diary.title: Death of Kaloyan; the singers' war at the Wartburg
diary.details: Kaloyan's reign ends. In Germany the Landgrave of Thuringia (the book calls him margrave) holds a contest for the crown of poetry, on the terms that every losing singer must die; Henry of Ofterdingen loses to Wolfram von Eschenbach and is let go to fetch the one bard he says is better, Klingsohr.

diary.title: Sava returns to Studenica
diary.details: Sava, Nemanja's youngest son, who had left family politics for the monks of Mount Athos, comes back to Studenica and begins to organise the Serbian Orthodox Church.

diary.title: Hermann von Salza hochmeister; Simium writes to Polyaigos
diary.details: Hermann von Salza is elected hochmeister of the Teutonic Order. About this time Simium, headmaster of the Scholomance, begins writing to Polyaigos in the Theban Tribunal, a covenant that also prepares pupils before apprenticeship; an exchange is talked of, but old enmity between Thebes and Transylvania stands in its way. (The book says within the last ten years or so.)

diary.title: The Burzenland granted to the Teutonic Knights
diary.details: Straight after a marriage contract between King Andrew II and Landgrave Hermann of Thuringia for their children, Hermann von Salza's Order is invited to Transylvania (the book also credits a King Bela, and makes Hermann of Thuringia head of the Salza family). Andrew gives it the Burzenland, free of taxes and dues, keeping the right to mint and half the gold and silver mined, and charges it to hold the Carpathian passes against the Cumans. Brother Theoderich commands the mission; Saxon settlers follow in numbers, and the Knights begin five castles, Marienburg, Kronstadt, Rosenau, Schwarzenburg and Kreuzburg.

diary.title: Macrobius slain; Essedarius leads Kezdö Válasz
diary.details: Macrobius, filius of Gasparus and leader of Kezdö Válasz, is torn apart by an angry griffin he met by chance in the Prokletije, the Accursed Mountains. His filius Essedarius, the fourth leader in Norsius's line, takes command. Leona, his partner, was not with him; she hunts the beast down and still hunts griffins in her grief.

diary.title: The Valley of the Thracian Kings found
diary.details: A Tremere necromancer serving as a hoplite finds the burial ground of the ancient Thracian kings close to Seuthopolis, their old capital. Tremere's necromancers rejoice and House Verditius wants a dig too, since the Thracians honoured smith gods; Benilda, wary of cheerful necromancers, bars the way.

diary.title: Stefan the First-Crowned; Andrew II goes on crusade
diary.details: A papal legate crowns Stefan II king of all the Serbian and coastal lands, and most Serbian dioceses take up the Latin rite, though Kotor and Ston keep the Greek. Andrew II of Hungary sets out on crusade.

diary.title: Poena becomes Prima; Ivan Asen II tsar
diary.details: Poena becomes Prima of House Tremere, and Monica Ierne takes the post of legata, the House's field commander. The former Primus is given charge of the Burning Acorns Vexillation, which hunts surviving Diedne, a post that lets him roam as he pleases. Ivan Asen II takes the Bulgarian throne at Tarnovo and marries a daughter of the King of Hungary. Andrew II comes home from crusade to a hostile nobility (the book dates his return to 1222).

diary.title: Sava archbishop of an autocephalous Serbian Church
diary.details: At Sava's request the patriarch of the Greek Church makes the Serbian Church self-governing and consecrates Sava its archbishop. Sava's Nomocanon becomes the book of church law for all the Slav churches.

members.office: Chief aide to the secretary for contingencies
Troubleshooter for the secretary for operations

tribunals.secrets: If the saga follows history, Andrew II's nobles force the Golden Bull on him in 1222; the Mongols break the Cumans at the Kalka in 1223; Hermann von Salza has the Burzenland made a fief of the Holy See in 1225 and the Knights are driven out; Ivan Asen II spreads his rule over Thrace, Macedonia and Epiros within the decade; a crusade against Bosnia comes in 1237; and the Mongols invade in 1241.

neighbours.name: Pannonia's first site
neighbours.summary: Where Pannonia was founded, as a fortified covenant of House Tremere near the old meeting point of the Transylvanian, Greater Alps and Roman Tribunals. A powerful monastery was later built at the springs of the river the covenant drew its water from, and its Dominion destroyed the magic aura. Pannonia's magi scattered into camps, the first in the Tribunal to do so, and the magi of Old Histria now gather most of its old resources. The book gives no date and does not name the river or the monastery.

neighbours.name: Domostron's first site
neighbours.summary: The first home of Domostron, the covenant Tremere's Hermetic allies founded, later wrecked by raiders from the Theban Tribunal. The book gives neither date nor place; it is set here near the Theban border only as a guess.

neighbours.name: The Kal Valley and Lake Balaton
neighbours.summary: A secluded valley in the Tribunal's west, wild yet within reach of the great cities of Hungary and Italy. Hungarians use its name for the dullest place on earth, so a troupe can put anything there without disturbing the history it wants to keep. Close by lies Lake Balaton, the Tribunal's western gateway: never deeper than about three metres, ringed by rich farmland and on the main trade routes, so stories pass by its shores. One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: Cakoc
neighbours.summary: A town near the Kal Valley with an odd pull on dragons. Saint George killed a black beast here long ago and so ended the custom of feeding it girls. In 1220 a green dragon lives in the nearby mountains; it scares the folk and takes their sheep but does little worse, so no one knows whether it is Infernal. It can talk, though it seldom bothers, beyond telling a shepherd to keep his dog close or lose it (see the Bestiary for the dragons). One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: The Tomb of Attila
neighbours.summary: Somewhere under the bed of the Tisza lies Attila, king of the Huns, whom the Magyars count as their forefather and the founder of Buda. His people turned the river aside by a canal to bury him, his warriors cut themselves and rode about his body singing laments, and he was sealed in coffins of iron, silver and gold; then every labourer was killed so the place would be forgotten. Among his grave goods may be the Sword of Mars, a weapon fallen from the sky that let him scourge the world. One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: Klingsohr's fields by the Tisza
neighbours.summary: The plain near the Tisza where the hidden bard Klingsohr wanders in peasant clothes, singing of Hungary's beauty to the empty fields. In 1207 the Margrave of Thuringia held a contest at Wartburg for the title of king of poetry, the losers to be put to death; Wolfram von Eschenbach beat Henry of Ofterdingen, who lamented that the one bard better than both was absent. Henry followed the songs that drift through Hungary's leaves, birds and storm clouds, which settle in the mind unbidden, and found Klingsohr, who cared nothing for prizes but came to save Henry's life. Crowned with bay by Wolfram, he had the death sentences lifted and foretold the Margrave's family's fate, which has come true in every point. He still foretells what is to come for anyone in need of it, or kind to him. One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: The Sunken City
neighbours.summary: A Roman city that slid almost whole into the Black Sea, tied in ancient times to astronomers and their Mysteries. A covenant here would reach easily into Greek culture and trade, the Tribunal's heart and the lands east of the Order; many Black Sea islands nearby have strange myths of their own. On a modern map it is near Kavarna. One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: The Isle of Achilles
neighbours.summary: A small Black Sea island where Achilles was buried. His temples are fallen, but since some mystical event in Roman times his spirit, Helen's and those of some of their followers dwell there. No woman may land, and men only by day, sleeping aboard ship if they stay longer; Achilles kills any visitor of Trojan blood, and Trojan princes settled as far as Rome and Britain. Fishermen use it as a safe anchorage in storms, if they dare. Tremere and their companions come to talk war with Achilles, calmer now than in life, and others ask Helen where ancient cities and temples lay; some scholars think the two are the heart of a mystery cult, though House Tremere has no record of one. Most tellers place Achilles' grave elsewhere, but the local folk and several ancient authors put it here. One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: The Seventy-Seventh Island
neighbours.summary: The seventy-seventh island of the Black Sea lies under a darkness so thick a spoon would stand up in it. At its heart grow three reeds: in the middle one is trapped a maiden said to be the fairest in the world, and in the other two her handmaids. A witch guards them who must die the moment the Reed Maiden goes free. Only a steed raised on dragon's milk, fed live coals and given fire to drink can pierce the dark. One of chapter one's sites suggested for a new oppidum.

neighbours.name: Hungary
neighbours.summary:
The Magyar kingdom that holds the north of the Tribunal. Even beyond its borders, nobles of Hungarian blood and Hungarian quarters in the larger towns are common. King Andrew II rules it from a triangle of three court cities, Esztergom, Székesfehérvár and Veszprém, between which his court travels.

The royal lands are cut into 72 counties (megye), each run from a fortified town of earth banks, ditch and timber wall by a count (ispán) the king appoints; most counts hold several and send deputies, the curial counts, to the rest. A count lives on peasant rents and a third of his county's taxes, tolls and fines, and ranks with a bishop. Private castles are against the law and stone ones almost unknown. Frontier counts guard marches of log and earth barriers, with an empty border zone beyond, watched by Szekler and Pecheneg horse archers. The fringes have no counties: a voivode governs Transylvania, a ban governs Croatia, and the Dalmatian cities rule themselves by treaty with the Crown.

Andrew's 'new institutions' set twenty barons, chosen from the high nobility, above the counts: first the palatine, the judge royal, the ban of Croatia and the voivode of Transylvania, then the queen's and the chamber's masters, then the masters of horse, table and cup. He has given them huge royal estates, to arm them like western knights say his friends, to buy them and pay his crusade debts say his foes; since Hungarian land owes neither service nor tax, the gift goes further than any in France or Germany. Foreign settlements outside the counts' reach and the new class of freed royal servants have both cut into the counts' power.

Hungarians are reserved, courteous and stiff about the precedence birth gives them; they put the family name first and never talk of money, though no other subject is forbidden. Serfs are chattels; most free men are still bound to fight or work for a lord, and only the gentry and foreigners enjoy 'golden freedom'. Castle folk, castle warriors, the half-free royal serfs (udvornici) and the villages that owe the court one fixed trade or good (conditionarii) fill out the ranks, and hospites, guests such as the Saxons and Szeklers, live under their own laws. Any landholder counts as noble, and the gentry claim descent from 108 pagan chieftains of the conquest; the question of who is noble is still open, and the Golden Bull of 1222 may settle it on land, which would make most magi nobles without any oath. Villages are small and shifting, famine is almost unknown (the Quaesitors once checked for Hermetic meddling), and wheat is cheap.

The king's wealth rivals any in Christendom: if Andrew is as rich as his grandfather Béla, a third of it comes from reminting the coin each year at the one royal mint in Esztergom, the rest from tolls, the counties' taxes, the salt monopoly, the Saxons, the counts' yearly gift and the Slavonians. All mines are his, and he takes a tenth of the gold panned in Transylvania. Making metal or coin by magic robs that revenue and could bring a royal army down on an oppidum; the Order would not protect the culprit.

The Holy Crown. Hungarians hold that their crown, kept at Székesfehérvár, is a living Divine being linking God and man, ruling the land for the Virgin Mary, to whom Saint Stephen gave it; the kingdom is its body, all Hungarians are equal beneath it, and even a king may be lawfully resisted if he gives land to foreigners, meddles with others' land, brings in new kinds of justice, tramples the rights of natives or foreigners, or fails to defend the faith. Magi who stand against corrupt nobles have sometimes been helped by miracles. It is the Crown, not the king, that guarantees the magi their right to be judged by the Code; it intervenes rarely, but far more readily than any mortal king, and the Order dare not fail to police its own.

No witches. King Coloman the Learned decreed in the eleventh century that witches do not exist and none may be tried; the Quaesitors found no magus behind it. The Order's magic counts in law as the custom of an ancient people, so magi keep their own laws and judges, as Saxons, crusading orders and Pechenegs do. The great nobles know of magi and bring complaints to Redcap envoys in discreet town mansiones, but do not tell a magus from a village cunning man, so the Tribunal polices hedge wizards too; a hedge wizard in deep trouble may claim trial under the Ancient Custom, though the Code punishes harder than any Hungarian court.

The Church came with Saint Stephen as a tool of royal power and has stamped out paganism except among the Cumans. Every ten villages must build and furnish a church; laws on Christian conduct are harsh (talking in church earns a whipping), church lands are under royal protection, but paganism now draws only a fast, and Jews and Muslims serve the king in coinage and the treasury unhindered. Orthodox Romanians pay a sheep tax, the fiftieth, instead of tithe.

Vis (each in its place): Gyogy-to (Ignem and Aquam), and Laniena's Aggtelek caves: Baradla (Imaginem and Muto), Dobsinska (Ignem) and Ochtinska (Rego).

Horror seed: if history holds, the Mongols come in waves in the middle of the century, a horde that can only be fled, not beaten (see The Mongols).

a giant kept chained in a barrel in some king's palace

neighbours.name: Gyogy-to
neighbours.summary: The biggest warm lake in Europe, beside Hévíz in the west of the kingdom. It yields both Ignem and Aquam vis, and as far as anyone knows, unlike many hot springs, it has no tie to Hell. There are traces of magic worked here by Romans and peoples before them. It lies just far enough from the Redcaps' road to Histria that no mansio stands here. A good site for a new oppidum; the book gives no aura.

neighbours.name: The Aggtelek Caves
neighbours.summary: A cluster of limestone caves in the hills of northern Hungary, beautiful beyond words, many of them with a Magic aura. Laniena stands at the mouth of the greatest, Baradla, and gathers vis from three of them. Some passages are thought to join one cave to another.

neighbours.name: Baradla Cave
neighbours.summary:
The largest and grandest of the Aggtelek caves, with the strongest aura of them, Magic 5: more than sixteen miles of winding galleries, dead ends and hidden chambers, crowded with columns, flowstone and dripstone streaked red, green and violet, some of it slumped as though the rock had softened like candle wax. Imaginem and Muto vis are both found here (Laniena's).

Only Lexander has explored it at length, and not all of it; he has warded every entrance he knows, because he turns vampires, werewolves and other captured horrors loose in the maze and sends his pupils after them.

neighbours.name: Dobsinska Cave
neighbours.summary: A cave further north, entered by a single sheer shaft the locals call the studena diera, the cold hole, for the cave is full of ice even at midsummer; few will climb down for fear of freezing in its depths. Laniena gathers Ignem vis here. The book gives its aura no number.

neighbours.name: Ochtinska Cave
neighbours.summary: One of the smallest caves and one of the strangest: its roof and walls sprout the 'flowers of iron', white tufts of stony needles like sea urchins. They are Rego vis, and also lesser enchantment vis that gives whoever bears one a personal Ward Against Faeries of the Earth (level 10, Penetration 10). Laniena's. The book gives its aura no number.

neighbours.name: The Estate of the Wizards
neighbours.summary: A mansio in Esztergom kept by House Mercere where travelling magi may stay: a graceful three-storey house like a Roman villa, older than any record, which its people say once stood outside the town; the city has grown round it, and it now sits in a ring of formal gardens. Nobles who have a grievance against magi bring it here, and when the king's judges and the magi's servants dispute who should try a case, they argue it out here. That magi deal with mundanes through servants is an old right the Holy Crown protects. Other mansiones, public and private, are scattered about the Tribunal.

neighbours.name: Kingdom of Hungary
neighbours.summary:
King Andrew (Endre, Andreas) II of the house of Árpád, who came home from the Fifth Crusade in 1218 deep in debt after raising the biggest crusading army ever seen. He is pushing through his 'new institutions', handing royal land and power to a new rank of barons to make the realm stronger in war; the reform is half done and may prove a mistake, and the old nobility resents both the barons and the king's freed royal servants. He farms out offices for cash and is thinking of auctioning the mint itself.

The king's own lands, the largest in the kingdom, are blocks of villages around royal manors (curtes), much of them royal forest kept by villages of foresters under a procurator. Unlike his nobles, the king does not split his lands among his sons. He is crowned by the Archbishop of Esztergom, at Székesfehérvár. The Church scolds him for his tolerance of Muslims, pagans and Jews. If history runs its course, his nobles force the Golden Bull on him in 1222.

neighbours.name: The Palatine of Hungary
neighbours.summary: First of the king's twenty barons, ranking with the judge royal, the ban of Croatia and the voivode of Transylvania above the rest. Barons are drawn from the high nobility and each holds at least one county; the king can remove one from office only by giving him something as rich. The book does not name the palatine.

neighbours.name: Archbishopric of Esztergom
neighbours.summary: Head of the Hungarian Church, enthroned in the basilica of Saint Adalbert, who baptised the royal house, on the crown of Esztergom's castle hill. He alone may crown the king. In name the Church stands with the Crown; in truth it is loudly critical of the king's leniency to Muslims, pagans and Jews, and the royal palace next door keeps the quarrel quiet. A Count of the Mint who keeps the Muslim minters would clash with him. The archbishopric is among the Church's richest landholders, and the bishops of the realm answer to it or to Kalocsa. Magi value the bishops of Veszprém as a weight against him.

neighbours.name: Archbishopric of Kalocsa
neighbours.summary: The second of Hungary's two archbishoprics, junior to Esztergom; part of the realm's bishops answer to it. With Esztergom it holds the largest church lands in the kingdom, and in theory it is a close ally of the king.

neighbours.name: Bishopric of Veszprém
neighbours.summary: The first bishopric of Hungary, founded by Saint Stephen. Its bishop has the old right to crown the queen; when another bishop crowned the present queen, the quarrel split the Hungarian Church until the Pope stepped in and confirmed Veszprém's right. Pannonhalma nearby is older and richer, so this is the poorest and weakest of the ancient sees, and its bishops usually stand close to the Order, which values them as a counterweight to the Archbishop of Esztergom.

neighbours.name: Bishopric of Pécs
neighbours.summary: One of the two bishoprics, with Oradea, whose lands are among the largest the Church holds in Hungary after the two archbishoprics.

neighbours.name: Bishopric of Oradea
neighbours.summary: A great landholding see (the book's Ordea), which keeps the Divine Dexter, Saint Stephen's mummified right hand, one of the kingdom's holiest relics.

neighbours.name: The Cathedral Chapter of Székesfehérvár
neighbours.summary: The richest and mightiest cathedral chapter in Hungary, in Saint Stephen's basilica. It guards the Holy Crown, a living Divine being, and the tombs of the kings. Its provost ranks with a count, and archdeacons run each of its counties for him.

neighbours.name: The Abbey of Pannonhalma
neighbours.summary: The biggest and wealthiest monastery in Hungary, a Benedictine house older than the see of Veszprém nearby and the mother house of many others; in 1200 it ruled 2,200 households. Its wealth is one reason Veszprém is poor.

neighbours.name: Esztergom
neighbours.summary:
The capital and biggest city of Hungary (the book's Esztergorm), an old camp of the Romans, of Attila and of the first Magyar king, where the roads to Kiev, Constantinople and Regensburg meet. The castle hill above the river holds the royal palace, built by western masons a few decades ago and the wonder of the realm, where foreign kings are always received, on the site of Saint Stephen's birthplace, so he is thought to watch closely over his heirs here; and the archbishop's basilica of Saint Adalbert. About 11,000 live in the town below, many of them foreign: craftsmen the king has hired and merchants, since the law makes every foreign trader offer his goods here first.

The Order's mansio, the Estate of the Wizards, stands here amid its gardens. Here too is the realm's only mint, whose Khwarezmian minters (the kaliz) are sharp at spotting false coin: magi who make coins of created silver are likelier to be caught here than in any other Tribunal.

Story seeds: the king, drowning in crusade debt, auctions the office of Count of the Mint each year, and magi could buy it openly or through a front, lawfully under the Code, though they must then hunt forgers and tax the miners; if they do not, a syndicate backed by Venetian bankers wins it, perhaps with House Mercere's domus magna behind it, and later the king splits the right among new mints at Csanád, Szerem, Buda and Zagreb. A faerie forger strikes coins bearing magi's sigils and oppida's marks. A royal coin inspector vanishes, perhaps tortured for his tests for forgery, and oppida race to find him for the king's favour or his secrets.

neighbours.name: Székesfehérvár
neighbours.summary: A city ringed by marsh, fortified by the first Magyar king, where Saint Stephen built a basilica and set a bishop; it has grown into the realm's centre of church learning, full of monasteries and churches and the largest cathedral school in the kingdom. Not the capital, but the city of ceremony: kings are always crowned here and, if they can be, buried here; pilgrimages begin here, the nobles meet here in their diets, and the regalia, the Holy Crown above all, are kept here, while the treasury proper is at Esztergom.

neighbours.name: Veszprém
neighbours.summary: The smallest of the three court cities, its castle older than the Magyar conquest; Saint Stephen's queen loved it, and he founded Hungary's first bishopric here. It is home to the college that trains the king's diplomats, whose library is one of the best in the land. If the Dragon War comes, dragons may try to burn it.

neighbours.name: The College of Veszprém
neighbours.summary: Where royal envoys learn their trade: the liberal arts and law are taught. With Mostre's school in Bosnia it is the nearest thing the Tribunal has to a university. Its library, among Hungary's finest, has served more than one magus, by lucky browsing or quiet borrowing.

neighbours.name: The Cathedral School of Székesfehérvár
neighbours.summary: The largest cathedral school in the kingdom.

neighbours.name: The Barons of Hungary
neighbours.summary: The twenty great officers of Andrew's new institutions, ranked by their titles above the counts and enriched with vast royal estates. The old counts and the gentry resent them, and the strain between old nobles and the king's newly freed men is growing; the quarrel may end in the Golden Bull.

details.wants: Royal land, office and precedence; the old nobility wants them curbed
details.offers: Armed retinues in the western style

neighbours.name: The Kaliz
neighbours.summary: The king's minters, all Khwarezmian Muslims (Hungarians call every minter kaliz), with some thirty villages of Turks and many Jews in royal service in trade, coinage and the treasury; the Lateran Council's rules against them are not enforced. The Church dislikes them, and magi who stamped coin by magic and let them go might please the archbishop.

details.wants: To keep the mint and the king's favour
details.offers: Skill at minting and at catching forgers

neighbours.name: Bulgaria
neighbours.summary:
The Second Bulgarian Empire, which in 1220 holds most of the Balkans between the Black Sea and the Morava, and Wallachia beyond the Danube too. Its capital is Tarnovo; Niš, Sredets and Silistra are its great cities, and Varna and Nesebar its ports. Its young tsar, Ivan Asen II, means to win back the old empire's glory, and if the saga follows history he will within ten years master Thrace, Macedonia and Epiros and push west into Serbian lands as far as Belgrade.

The land has always lived by its roads: the Danube and the Romanian plain carry trade from the Bosphorus to Central Europe, and so does the old highway by Adrianople, Plovdiv, Sredets, Niš and Belgrade. The fertile Danube lowlands in the north feed the empire; the Stara Planina runs across its middle; south of it lie the Sredets and Thracian plains, divided at the Gates of Trajan; and the Rila, Pirin and Rhodope ranges close the south.

Thracians, Romans, Goths and Slavs all settled it before Khan Asparukh's Bulgars crossed the Danube in 679 to 681 and built the First Bulgarian Empire, which lasted until Byzantium swallowed it in 1018. Krum took Hungary and Transylvania in 803 and died suddenly in 814 after beating two emperors and besieging Constantinople; Boris was baptised about 870 as Michael; Symeon took the title of tsar and gave the Church its own head in 926. Pechenegs, Magyars and Uzes followed. The brothers Teodor Petar, Ivan Asen and Kaloyan broke Byzantine rule in 1185, and Kaloyan, who reigned from 1197 to 1207, rebuilt the empire.

Bulgarians are stocky and dark, hard-working, tolerant and welcoming, steadier than the Serbs but stubborn fighters for a cause they think just. The men wear loose trousers tucked into tall boots, the women bright skirts, and both embroidered shirts with waistcoats or bodices.

Hermetically, three oppida lie here: Evredika, the scattered sancta of the Cult of Orpheus in the Rhodopes; Seuthopolis, the Quaesitors' town near the Shipka Pass, where the Tribunal meets; and Tablinum, the museum of regiones in the Danube delta. Gigas, the Theban Tremere lodge south-west of Sofia, lies just over the border.

Vis here (each in its place): the silivriak of the Rhodopes (Imaginem) and the bones of the Devil's Throat (Corpus), both Evredika's; Tablinum's Vim distillery; and Starosel's Terram and Herbam, which no oppidum holds. From a mountain eyrie the powerful aždaja Rabidanadas watches the demon Akgah's success in the Theban Tribunal and dreams of leading a band of aždaje against the Bulgarian kingdom.

links.note: the Bulgarian demon that wears a corpse
a four-eyed dog, born to hunt vampires

neighbours.name: The Danube Delta
neighbours.summary: Where the Danube meets the Black Sea it spreads into a wilderness of swamp, reed beds and marsh covering perhaps a thousand square miles, home to vast flocks of white pelicans and egrets. South of it the Dobrudja is a dry country of sandy steppe and low hills full of copper, poor in a drought but very rich where it can be watered. Tablinum hides among the dunes and wetlands of the coast.

neighbours.name: The Galleries of Tarnovo
neighbours.summary: The Roman city of Nikopolis ad Istrum stood some twelve miles north of Tarnovo until the Huns sacked it in 447. Legend says its people fled to Trapezitsa Hill carrying the city's riches, dug passages deep into the rock, and hid the hoard there behind deadly traps. Treasure seekers have hunted it ever since, and the townsfolk fear its traps and its curse.
neighbours.secrets: A Tarnovo man who has found a tunnel beneath his house looks for foreign adventurers to explore it, since no local will go down; he means to cheat them of whatever gold they bring out.

neighbours.name: Baldwin's Tower
neighbours.summary:
A tower over Tarnovo's Frankish quarter, built to hold Baldwin, the Latin emperor of Constantinople, whom Tsar Kaloyan took in battle in 1205. Kept at first as a precious hostage, Baldwin ruined himself by courting Kaloyan's Cuman wife (or, some say, she charged him with rape when he refused her); he was bricked up inside, his cries carried over the quarter for months and then stopped, and the tsar told the pope he was dead.

Some say Kaloyan beheaded him and drank from his skull, and that his headless body, unburied, walks around the tower seeking vengeance on the Asens. At least one band of foreigners has tried to break in to free him, and failed: the tower cannot be forced.
neighbours.secrets: Others insist Baldwin still lives, a prisoner the present tsar keeps for some purpose of his own.

neighbours.name: The Stara Planina
neighbours.summary: The Old Mountains, Haemus to the ancients: a narrow chain running nearly four hundred miles west from the Black Sea through the heart of Bulgaria. High meadows feed sheep and cattle, beech woods cover the middle slopes, and the foothills are farmed. The range shields the Thracian Plain from the hard winters of the Romanian side.

neighbours.name: The Shipka Pass
neighbours.summary:
The best way through Bulgaria's mountains, near Seuthopolis. In the Order's early years Tremere himself fought a band of Theban magi here, and beside the battlefield lies a regio: some think it older than the fight and the place Tremere laid his ambush, others that the battle's strain threw some magus into Twilight and made it. For a long time afterwards House Tremere and the Theban covenants met in it to reflect and to sign treaties.

When House Guernicus took over the Tribunal site from the Praeco, and was asked to hold yearly Tribunals so that justice came quicker and trained apprentices were accepted sooner, the Quaesitors chose this regio: it was close to Seuthopolis and already had buildings. The full Tribunal every seven years is more a festival than a parliament, so the hall need not be large.

Groups of magi raise splendid temporary buildings on the valley's terraces, as lodgings, shops and places of amusement; new coloniae often first show themselves by pitching a tent on the Western Promenade, west of the hall, while visitors from other Tribunals, especially those with goods to sell, gather on the Eastern. Strolling the Promenades with friends, again and again with each circle one belongs to, is the great pleasure of a meeting, and newcomers are told to bring good boots. Redcaps race on foot between the two carved winged feet of Hermes that mark the regio's ends, and some take the races very seriously.

The Hall of the Tribunal is little more than an immense roof on plain columns of a Greek sort, a few carved in honour of magi who served the Order greatly, under a magically lit and richly decorated ceiling. Every magus of the Tribunal has a seat, in horseshoe rows around a dais, with room for a hundred more; on the dais stands the Praeco's oak throne, about whose making many tales are told. The servants of the visiting magi find the meetings full of romance, wagers, games and gossip.

levels.name: The Tribunal regio
levels.notes: The book gives no aura; 5 is the pack's. A terraced valley with the Hall of the Tribunal between the Western and Eastern Promenades, a giant winged foot of Hermes carved at each end.

neighbours.name: The Rila Mountains
neighbours.summary: The range south of Sredets, whose northern peak, Mount Vitosha, looms over the Sredets Plain; with the Pirin to the south it nearly meets the Stara Planina at the Gates of Trajan. Saint Ivan Rilski's monastery and his hermitage lie here, and the Seven Lakes high above.

neighbours.name: Ivan Rilski's Cave
neighbours.summary:
Saint Ivan Rilski (John of Rila), hermit, healer and mystic, who died in 946, lived twelve years in this cave, three in a hollow oak and seven on a high rock above it; the disciples his fame drew became the monastery that still stands. Cave, tree and rock each hold a Divine aura of 4, apart from the monastery's own Dominion aura of 3. The saint's uncorrupted body now lies at Tarnovo. Saint Ivan Rilski himself, Bulgaria's patron, is in the Bestiary.

Story seed: the monks speak for the nation's saint and sway the bolyeri, but before they grant a favour they may require the petitioners to repeat his life in little, twelve days in the cave, three in the oak and seven on the rock, while the saint tries the purity of their purpose. Those who pass may win the monastery's friendship; the same ordeal could serve as Initiation into a Holy Tradition of the saint.

neighbours.name: The Seven Lakes
neighbours.summary:
A chain of lakes high in the Rila Mountains, between about 6,900 and 8,200 feet, where faerie magic makes the water run from one lake to the next in no sensible order. The district has a Faerie aura of 3. A water-maiden vila, one of seven jealous sisters, lives in each lake (see the Bestiary); each offers a bather a faerie gift for a year and a day as her guest beneath the water, and must kill the guest on the last day.

Story seed: each sister's gift is a Minor Virtue with a Faerie Charm, and each can save the bearer from another sister's way of killing. Locals advise beginning at Babreka, whose gift sees through glamour and so defeats Dolnoto, the best illusionist; Dolnoto's gift, a lesser immunity to poison, is said to beat the sister who poisons her guests. Working out the order in which the water flows gives the order of the visits, and whoever wins all seven gifts is said to become the sisters' lord, owed their homage and obedience.

levels.name: The lake regiones
levels.notes: Each of the seven lakes has its own Faerie regio of 6, the home of its vila: top to bottom Salzata ('Tear'), Okoto ('Eye'), Babreka ('Kidney'), Bliznaka ('Twin'), Trilistnika ('Trefoil'), Ribnoto Ezero ('Fish Lake') and Dolnoto Ezero ('Lower Lake').

links.note: a template for the white ladies of the Tribunal

neighbours.name: Starosel
neighbours.summary:
A tomb temple of Bendis, the Thracian earth goddess, on the Thracian Plain, ringed by a wall of huge dressed stones carved with suns. The tomb is a mound reached by a broad stone stair to a landing; its cave-like door, framed in cut stone, opens on a plain antechamber and a splendid domed inner chamber painted with a bright frieze. It has a strong Magic aura of 6.

Vis: Terram and Herbam, gathered within a few yards of the temple (the book gives no amounts).

A fine site for a new oppidum, with ready-made and easily held walls, but it has a guardian: the place's genius loci, a hazy woman's shape of black earth and red clay with great power over earth, who can rouse the plants to help her and hates all change (see the Bestiary). Settlers must defeat or lastingly appease her; vis gatherers may strike a bargain to guard the temple for her in return. Starosel's genius loci, a magical spirit shaped like a woman of black soil and red clay with great power over earth and plants, guards the tomb temple and resists any change; settlers must master or pacify it for good, though vis gatherers may strike a bargain.
neighbours.secrets: The genius may or may not be the goddess once worshipped here; its Magic nature suggests not, and if so, something befell Bendis that settlers would be wise to learn first.

neighbours.name: The Madara Plateau
neighbours.summary: A plateau that rises from the Thracian Plain in a sheer cliff more than three hundred feet high, long holy to the Bulgar shamans, with a Faerie aura of 3. At its foot a path climbs to a great cave under an overhang, green with plants and watered by a small spring: a natural theatre where the old Bulgars honoured three water nymphs.

links.note: a giant's mother on her hidden horse farm
the faerie horse starved on Nicoleta's farm

neighbours.name: The Madara Horseman
neighbours.summary:
Seventy-five feet up the Madara cliff a vast relief shows a rider spearing a lion under his horse's hooves, with an eagle flying before him and a hound behind: one of the Bulgar shamans' gods. Close to the carving the Faerie aura rises to 5.

The right faerie rite wakes the Horseman, and his horse, hound and eagle, which are part of his glamour, with him; the lion, a faerie in its own right, wakes too, and he must fight and beat it while he lives. He guards the local people he swore to protect and goes at once against whatever he judges their worst danger. Neither he nor the Lion (Faerie Might 20 or more each, the Lion's matching his) can be killed for good: the legend is so strong that other faeries of the region take up their glamour and they can be called again.
neighbours.secrets: Story seed: a bolyar the magi know begs them to shelter him from the Horseman, loosed on him, he says, by a faerie wizard. In truth he paid the wizard to raise the Horseman against his enemies, but the Horseman had heard his people's prayers and judged the bolyar's pride and ambition the region's worst threat. The wizard only failed to warn him. If the magi let things run their course, the Lion may interfere.

neighbours.name: The Rhodope Mountains
neighbours.summary:
A tangle of ridges and valleys in the south, with summer pasture above woods of pine and fir, and since antiquity the heart of the worship of Orpheus and of Zagreus (the Greeks' Dionysus), Thrace's two great gods. The magi of Evredika keep their scattered sancta here in caves, stout houses and hidden stone towers.

The silivriak, the Orpheus flower, grew from the singer's blood when the Maenads killed him: its pink bell flowers spring up anew each year even from a plant dried or scorched in a fire, and the year's first blooms give Evredika Imaginem vis. A vis-bearing flower is a Plant of Virtue that can be Enriched: write a poem each day for ninety days and recite them to it, then crush it and anoint three strings of an old-style lyre with its juice. The lyre gives its player Enchanting Music 3, effective only on the bereaved, which cannot be improved and replaces the player's own score; each broken string (on a botch, say) takes away a point for good.

neighbours.name: Gela
neighbours.summary: Evredika's: a small village in the central Rhodopes, the legendary birthplace of Orpheus. The Cult of Orpheus keeps a sanctum here, usually held by a magus with the Gentle Gift, who has a yearly grant of vis from the oppidum (as a Personal Vis Source) and in return must teach music and performance to anyone who asks. The village is now known for its musicians and draws pupils, Gifted and not, from the whole region. The magi of Evredika gather once a year in a green meadow near it, ringed by mountains, when the silivriak blooms.

neighbours.name: The Devil's Throat
neighbours.summary:
Evredika's: Diavolsko Garlo, a great cave into which a waterfall plunges far underground, said (though other places make the same claim) to be the door to Hades that Orpheus used to seek Eurydice. The Thracians once threw their dead kings down the fall to speed them to the afterlife. At the bottom the water pools in a still, dark lake, and on its shore, in the din of the falls, is the sanctum that by custom belongs to the oppidum's Tremere aedile. Magic aura 4.

The Orphic magi, who take Orpheus's descent as a journey of the spirit, care little for the site; they hold it for its history, and for the Corpus vis that now and then washes up on the lake shore as pieces of old skeletons.

neighbours.name: Perperikon
neighbours.summary:
Evredika's: a stone city on a hilltop in the eastern Rhodopes, once a great shrine of Zagreus, left empty by ordinary folk for centuries. The small town that has grown at the foot of the hill calls it the City of Ghosts; Evredika's covenfolk secretly live among the ruins and may account for some of the tales. Magic aura 3.

At its centre is an oval hall with a round altar on a stone dais: the oracle of Zagreus-Dionysus where Alexander learnt he would conquer Asia. A line of minor hedge wizards still takes auguries there the old way, pouring wine on the altar, setting it alight and reading the future in the flames; these priests are initiates of Divination and Augury who chiefly use pyromancy.

neighbours.name: The Rock Womb
neighbours.summary:
Evredika's: a cave near Perperikon shaped like a womb, with a carved altar at its far end. At noon a shaft of sun through a hole cut in the roof throws the shape of a phallus on the floor, and in January and February, with the sun low, on the altar itself; then the cave fills with a strong Magic aura of fertility (the book gives no number). Childless women come to lie with strangers here to conceive, and the children often carry magical blood.

A magus seeking the lost Fertility Magics may find Insight here, for instance by watching by magic the whole growth in the womb of a child conceived in the cave, which might show how to align children to Supernatural Virtues or Abilities.

neighbours.name: The Caverns of Seuthopolis
neighbours.summary: Seuthopolis's: under the fortified town lie the caverns of the old Thracian cult, with a Magic aura of 5 save in a few places. The magi use part of them for laboratories and libraries.

neighbours.name: The Crypt of the Martyred Virgin
neighbours.summary: Seuthopolis's: a vault in the caverns, hallowed by a martyred virgin's bones (Divine aura 3) and wrapped in layer on layer of magical defences. The Red and Black Libraries are kept here together, which troubles even magi who accept that they must exist; the Quaesitors answer that the vault cost a fortune and could not easily be built again.

neighbours.name: The Valley of the Thracian Kings
neighbours.summary:
The burial ground of the kings of ancient Thrace, close to Seuthopolis, their old capital, found four years ago by a Tremere necromancer then serving as a hoplite (the book gives no aura). House Tremere's necromancers were delighted; House Verditius wants to dig too, since the Thracians worshipped gods of the forge. Benilda, minding an old saying never to trust a happy necromancer, keeps everyone out for now, knowing Tremere will win in the end; she hopes to look first herself, or to steer who digs and why.

Saga seed: an excavation must be hidden from mundanes, get past cunningly trapped tombs, calm guardian spirits the magician kings left and the diggers wake, judge the magic items among the grave goods and whether they help Original Research, and learn of the Cabeiri, the Thracians' gods, and the powers they gave their servants, perhaps by journeys into the Magic or Faerie realms or by seeking Initiation into their Mysteries. In the Valley of the Thracian Kings a faerie calling itself Kabeiros, a tall brass man with a crab's claw for a left hand, is reviving the Cabeiri cult here, initiating Quaesitors' servants into Eyes of Theseus and the other cult Virtues.
neighbours.secrets:
The false Kabeiros (see the Bestiary), a strong local faerie, is reviving the Cabeiri cult here: a tall brass man with a great crab claw for a left hand, which serves him as smith's tongs and to punish the unjust. He courts the servants of Quaesitors, posing as the guide of kings and giver of justice. His cult has four degrees (Interrogator, Invader, Observer, Liberator), all initiated in the valley on a holy day under a Vow to give fair and swift justice; they confer Piercing Gaze, Invasive Eyes, Bright Eyes and Eyes of Theseus, and he can take back Eyes of Theseus from the disloyal. He wants to teach Second Sight but has not yet stolen it from anyone.
He took the idea from a cult of servants at a Quaesitorial covenant who long ago worshipped Asmodeus as patron of prying; an Infernal scholar of the Black Library might trace it, and Asmodeus may punish the cult if he learns his idea was reused.

neighbours.name: Tablinum
neighbours.summary:
On the Black Sea coast among the dunes and marshes of the Danube delta: to the eye only a palisaded village of a few grogs of Slav stock who fish from small boats amid clouds of pelicans and egrets. All that marks it is an Aegis of the Hearth of magnitude 8 round the palisade and a magic bell for calling the magi, which makes no sound except within Tablinum's regiones.

Here dozens of regiones lie on top of one another, each an exhibition hall: stone buildings joined by covered wooden walkways, vaulted halls under twisting brass chandeliers, narrow dark passages lined with scroll cases, alike in style but different in plan from level to level. The levels can be sensed but not crossed into by any path or ritual; one goes in only with an Arcane Connection and Leap of Homecoming or the like. The Curator holds Fixed Arcane Connections to most of them, stone beads on necklaces handed down from Curator to Curator, and by holding them controls who sees what. Unless noted, the levels can be entered and left by Rego Corpus magic.

Outside the halls, where any opening exists, the light is a thick red, as of a summer evening or dawn, with no sun in the sky; featureless dunes surround the buildings and the Black Sea heaves to the east, its salt wind crusting the eastern walls. Every path through the dunes leads back to the halls. Some say other, perhaps ruined, buildings hide among the dunes on some levels.

The Everbright Chandeliers that light the exhibits are enchanted items (CrIg 24, constant): they give bright light as from candles, with no flame to set the exhibits alight.

levels.name: The Art Exhibits
levels.notes: Open: Tremere by right, others by the Curator's leave. Fifteen exhibits, one to each Art, each on its own level, each a realia of hundreds of objects (the Corpus halls full of skeletons and pickled organs, flasks foul and pure in the Aquam, caged beasts behind Circles of Beast Warding in the Animal). Study Bonus and Study Requirement are met here up to an Art of 15.

levels.name: The Arcanum Exhibit
levels.notes: Open: Tremere by right, others by the Curator's leave. Four separate realia, on Finesse, Magic Theory, Parma Magica and Penetration: star maps of horoscopes' effect on Magic Resistance, glassware assemblies, rune-covered magical eggs whose runes writhe and slip.

levels.name: The Scriptorium
levels.notes: Not an exhibit: lodgings for guests' servants and companions (visiting magi live in the exhibit they study), a guest laboratory with a viewing gallery, and six scribes (Profession: Scribe 6, Magic Theory 1) copying the Chronicle. Up to two may be hired for 2 pawns a season, materials extra; a Tremere may take one free, though not two seasons running; writing desks are free. A small door leads to the Spell Hall.

levels.name: The Spell Hall
levels.notes: Open: Tremere by right, others by the Curator's leave. Archive Lab Texts in filed scroll cases: every ArM5 spell, most from the supplements, few originals, mostly free of private notation. Tremere copy freely; others donate a usable Lab Text (copying as many texts as its magnitude) or pay pawns equal to the magnitudes copied. No laboratory; texts may not leave, though the residents take them anyway.

levels.name: The Chronicle
levels.notes: Open: Tremere by right, others by the Curator's leave. Three copies of each of the 90 volumes of the Transylvania Chronicle; one copy of a volume may be taken out at a time. Anyone may study it.

levels.name: The Chapel
levels.notes: Open: Tremere by right, others by the Curator's leave. The Divine exhibit, a realia in Dominion Lore: glowing crosses hang in place of chandeliers over mosaics of Christ's life, and jewelled reliquaries fill the alcoves, dozens or hundreds of relics among them, perhaps an uncatalogued piece of the True Cross. The relics' Divine aura has drowned whatever aura the level once had.

levels.name: The Curator's Sanctum
levels.notes: Nominally open; the residents' lodgings and six laboratories, four in use, under the usual sanctum law. Nestor's laboratory here is a sham.

levels.name: The Mirrored Hall
levels.notes: Restricted: Tremere with good reason; others sometimes, for a fee. Hundreds of enchanted metal mirrors in warded iron frames, each holding a faerie in its reflection: a realia in Faerie Lore.

levels.name: The Dungeon
levels.notes: Restricted: Tremere with good reason; others sometimes, for a fee. A maze of dark passages displaying horrors of cruelty and suffering: a realia in Infernal Lore that many magi want destroyed. It holds more objects than any other exhibit, far more than the catalogues say, as anyone who studies it a season realises.

levels.name: The Empty Halls
levels.notes: Many empty regiones of vacant halls among the dunes, with Magic auras of 3 or 4; some say people have been stranded or imprisoned in them.

neighbours.secrets:
Six hidden exhibits are rumoured, which most of the Tribunal only guesses at; some magi claim to have been there, and may be liars or mad. Even the Curator may not hold their Arcane Connections, which a cabal or Mystery Cult may keep, or which may be lost:
The Founder's Exhibit: realia of the Founders' lives, first traditions and deaths, some say with several Founders' bodies on show.
The Lower Dungeon: a web of wards binding hundreds of demons; its keepers would risk a charge of infernalism.
The Refuge: not an exhibit but stocked laboratories and lodgings in hidden regiones, readied for House Tremere to flee to should catastrophe strike the House, the Tribunal or the world, and outlast it. Hidden laboratories do exist (Nestor uses one); if disaster such as the Mongols comes, desperate magi will come here.
The Schism Exhibit: a full record of the Schism War, including Expurgatio, said to catalogue all the evidence House Tremere gathered against the Diedne in the decades before the war, with the artifacts and Lab Texts it names; called 'the truth', against a public record many think Tremere propaganda.
The Seeker's Forum: realia of extinct (and not so extinct) magical traditions the Tremere have recovered across Mythic Europe, a rich source of Insight.
The Warehouse of Ares: a great store of magic weapons, many made by both sides around the Schism War, kept against the day the Order splits in war again.

neighbours.name: Tsardom of Bulgaria
neighbours.summary:
The Second Bulgarian Empire. Its ruler styles himself Emperor and Autocrat of all Bulgarians and Vlachs, lord of a people rather than of lands. Ivan Asen II, nephew of Kaloyan, has reigned only two years but already shows promise, beginning with his marriage to the King of Hungary's daughter; he is aggressive and set on restoring the empire. Kaloyan's Cuman marriage gave the tsars an alliance with the Cumans that must be renewed by rite each summer, and the empire still fights with Cuman mercenaries.

The tsar rules through the bolyeri, a hundred noble families of great and lesser bolyars; the great bolyars and the Patriarch form the Sinklit, the council that advises him. The land is divided into horas under a kefaliya (a duke), each with one or more katepans (counts) ruling katepanikons. (Duke is the app's highest title.)

No one doubts the Asens' right to rule, but no one knows what it rests on: the brothers came from nowhere to lead the revolt, and while most think them Bulgarian, some say Vlach or even Cuman. Their obscure past worries many, the Order among them, and their strange and seemingly inherited power to sway crowds is something to fear, or to use.

neighbours.name: The Archbishopric of Tarnovo
neighbours.summary:
The head of the Bulgarian Church, at the Patriarshiya on the top of Tsarevets Hill. The Church traces itself to Saints Cyril and Methodius, whom Boris I welcomed in 886; Constantinople granted it its own patriarch after the peace of 927, and took that away in 1018, when it shrank to an archbishopric at Ohrid led by Greek clergy.

The Asens restored its independence with a new archbishopric at their capital, and when the Patriarch of Constantinople would not accept it they turned to Rome: in 1203 Innocent III named the Archbishop of Tarnovo Primate of all Bulgaria and Wallachia, joining it to the Latin Church, though Ohrid stays Orthodox. Tsar and archbishop are thought still to be seeking union with the Orthodox, on their own terms.

neighbours.name: The Monastery of Saint Ivan Rilski, Rila
neighbours.summary: The community that grew from the disciples of Saint Ivan Rilski, with a Dominion aura of 3 apart from the Divine 4 of his cave, oak and rock. Its monks, thought to speak for the nation's patron saint, carry great weight in Bulgarian politics, and may set those who want their help the saint's own ordeal.

neighbours.name: The Monastery of Saint Ivan Rilski, Tarnovo
neighbours.summary: Within the walls of Trapezitsa Hill in Tarnovo, keeping the uncorrupted body of Saint Ivan Rilski, Bulgaria's patron.

neighbours.name: The Church of Saint Dimitar, Tarnovo
neighbours.summary: On the north side of Trapezitsa Hill, dedicated to Demetrius of Thessaloniki: here the Asens declared their revolt against Byzantium and the founding of the Second Bulgarian Empire.

neighbours.name: The Church of Saint Sofia, Sredets
neighbours.summary: Built in the sixth century under Byzantine rule and lately made a bishop's seat of the Bulgarian Church, so that people have begun to call Sredets by the diocese's name, Sofia.

neighbours.name: The Boyana Church
neighbours.summary: A church at Sredets, the masterpiece of the city's craftsmen, whose frescoes Vasiliy, the Boyana Master, is still painting: the dome is done, with Christ, the Evangelists, the great feasts, the Passion and ten warrior saints, and he is now painting Saint Nicholas's life in eighteen panels in the narthex. His work moves men to tears; he is a Maestro, and like most of them notices little but his art.
neighbours.secrets: An angel has taken Vasiliy under its wing, while a demon has fixed on the parish priest through his pride in the work, and the congregation are caught between them. Vasiliy may sense the struggle and ask for help, or the angel may ask the characters, or the demon trick them, to finish off the other.

neighbours.name: Tarnovo
neighbours.summary:
The capital, in a loop of the Yantra, a Danube tributary, on two hills the river splits and almost encircles, running in a gorge often three hundred feet below the walls; the New Town (Nov Grad) lies between them by the river. Tsarevets, on the left bank, is a rough triangle behind a wall thirty feet high and ten thick with three gates: the main gate (Sechena skala) with its drawbridge, the Small Gate (Malka porta) with its covered tower facing Trapezitsa, and the Frankish Gate into the Frankhissar, where foreign merchants lodge. The tsar's palace has its own second wall; the Patriarshiya crowns the hill among a dozen more churches, many paid for by the tsar; and from Execution Rock (Lobnata skala) at the north end traitors are thrown into the river.

Trapezitsa, on the right bank, has a weaker wall along the hill's rim, its main gate on the south side, from which a road cut in the rock crosses the Yantra and the New Town to the Small Gate; within are Saint Ivan Rilski's monastery and, on the north slope, the Church of Saint Dimitar. Nobles keep houses on the hills; craftsmen live in the New Town and in Assenova on the right bank.

neighbours.name: Sredets (Sofia)
neighbours.summary: A chief city of the First Bulgarian Empire on the wide Sredets Plain under Mount Vitosha, famed for its craftsmen, its goldsmiths above all; since its Saint Sofia became a bishop's seat, people call it Sofia. The Boyana Church is here.

neighbours.name: Seuthopolis
neighbours.summary: The walled town over the Quaesitors' caverns, laid out like many small Bulgarian towns, under Bulgaria in name but paying homage to no noble. A council of five old men governs it in public: one each for the carpenters, shepherds, weavers and potters, and a leader chosen from the four, whose guild at once names another in his place. Its people are Greeks, Bulgars and mountain Slavs.

details.charter: A charter it says Diocletian granted

neighbours.secrets: The charter is a skilful forgery; the oppidum of Seuthopolis rules here.

neighbours.name: The Bogomils
neighbours.summary:
A dualist faith, risen in the tenth century, whose name means 'dear to God'; neither tsar nor Church has stamped it out, and it is notorious across Europe. Bogomils teach that God had two sons: the elder, Satanael, rebelled and made the lower heavens, the earth and mankind (God giving the souls), and bound Adam to pay him homage for the soil; the younger, Michael, came as the man Jesus and broke that bond, so Satanael had him crucified and raised the Church to bind men anew. Whatever society makes is thus Satan's: they refuse taxes, serfdom and war, shun churches, sacraments and holy symbols, and pray in houses, holding to the Gospels, some epistles, the Psalms and the Prophets.

They are led by the Protos, with four great fraternities (obshtini): the Bulgarian, the Romana, the Dragometsia of Macedonia and the Meliniqua of Serbia, each under a dedets, a kind of bishop, helped by starets, elders. Champions of the poor, they resist crown and Church from quiet refusal to open revolt, and their wandering preachers, who heal and drive out demons, have seeded movements far away, the Cathars of Provence among them.

A Divine faith outside Christianity: their gatherings usually raise a Dominion aura of Calm temper, at odds with the Orthodox Church's, that fades between services. Dedetsi and starets hold Wise One, dedetsi Temporal Influence too; their missionaries are often of a Holy Tradition or Mythic Companions, like the Cathar Perfecti but with Intervention or Adjuration in place of Transcendence.

details.rules: Viarvashti, the believers, give up meat, wine, wealth and begetting to seek perfection; slushateli, the listeners, live less strictly and may rise; savarsheni, the perfects, lead and teach. Women and men are equal.
details.wants: To free the poor from lords, taxes and the Church's hold on wealth and learning
details.offers: Healing, the casting out of demons, and the loyalty of the downtrodden

neighbours.name: The Sinklit
neighbours.summary: The Bolyar Council: the great bolyars of Bulgaria's hundred noble families, with the Patriarch, who advise the tsar on policy. A bolyar who needs a favour from the magi, or whom the magi need, most likely sits here or serves one who does.

details.wants: A say in the tsar's policy and the great bolyars' standing
details.offers: Counsel, troops and the lands of the hundred noble families

neighbours.name: The Slav Lands
neighbours.summary:
