creatures.name: Broukolak
creatures.how_many: a kind: the demons that wear corpses in Bulgaria
creatures.weakness: Protected Group (those born on a Saturday)

powers.name: Form of Wickedness
powers.description: Reveals its true horror (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Form of Man
powers.description: Wears the dead man's face (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Contagious Obsession
powers.description: A point for each victim (Realms of Power: The Infernal).

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Costs 1 to 3 points: the Obsession Trait Fear.

powers.name: Burning Spittle
powers.description: Spits liquid fire as far as five paces: +10 damage if it penetrates, and whatever parries it is eaten away and ruined.

vis.where: in its teeth (the book gives no Art)

creatures.appearance: Like anyone else until it uses its powers; then a hunchback with glossy black skin, black hands and long nails, a peeling blood-red face, a cat's or wolf's teeth and wild hair and beard. As a shapeshifter it is mostly a cat, a goat or an owl.
creatures.notes: The Bulgarian name for the demon the Greeks call vrykolakas (The Sundered Eagle has it too): it devours a corpse and wears its shape. What draws a faerie vampire can draw it, but a curse at the moment of death is surest, and some wicked people curse themselves as they die. It sets up in trade in a village where no one knows it, eats and drinks first from the dead man's relatives, then further off, and the district's health declines as it feeds by night on beasts and people. It likes lone victims, grapples and bites, and may keep one alive for nightly feeding with scuffle damage. Its Spittle has no Defense. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal ch. 8

creatures.name: Minor Vila
creatures.how_many: a template: the white ladies, cast to suit each role
creatures.appearance: A lovely young woman, naked or dressed in white.
creatures.notes:
A weak vila fit for stories with grogs, or as a player character; she needs powers and more Might to be much use, and any Virtue added must be balanced by a Flaw (antagonists need not balance). The book's Human Form is the catalog's Humanoid Faerie. Her Might Form is usually Corpus. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
Powers by role (all Greater unless marked; in a hurry, double the Might cost and quadruple the Init penalty): shapeshifting into a falcon, horse, serpent, swan or wolf (2 to 4 points); the Enthralling Voice set (Allure 1, Enthralling Sound 3, Enthrallment 4, Guide 3, Kiss of Forgetfulness 4, Steal Judgment 2); the Blessing Dance (Grant a Major Virtue 10, a Minor Virtue 5, Puissance 2); the Cursing Dance (a cursed dancing ring made as a trinket, 10 or 15); Spirit Away. Roles: the captured wife whose skin or feathers are hidden; the cloud or storm maiden (Flight, a Storms Focus Power up to level 25, Guide to lead travellers astray); the cursed lover whose admirers pine away or die in a set kind of accident; the huntress (Bow 5, Ride 5, a bow at Attack +9, Damage +7, Shake the Earth 3), who kills oath-breakers; the temptress (Allure, Illusory Home 4, Pine Away 3); the water maiden (Illusory Home, Kiss of the Mermaid 3 for breathing water); the weaver witch, whose loom seems to spin out foot and horse soldiers; the woodland maiden (Extend Glamour, Guide, a Manifestation Focus Power over beasts and plants, and powers turning victims into beasts (3) or things (5)); and the wise woman (a Healing Focus Power, and a show of prophecy).
Wards: many vilas have a Sovereign Ward against a strand of their own hair, which forces them back into their basic shape and stops them harming its holder. The hair is often a Minor External Vis source, so she cannot truly die while it lasts; a strong vila may have Residual Power, which carries the hair away when she falls. Food, cakes and ribbons left at the edges of woods, roads, rivers and wells ward a house or a village. Giants have vila daughters; vilas bear humans, vilas or witches; witches bear witches, giants or dragons.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal ch. 8

creatures.name: Silexa

powers.name: Hands of the Magical Animal
powers.description: Carries things as though she had hands, with Strength 5; doing anything but carrying needs concentration (a Personal Power).

creatures.appearance: A wolf with a coat the colour of flint.
creatures.notes:
Monica Ierne's familiar (Monica's sheet has the bond). An Irish wolf rather than one of the native white wolves, she is a senior member of the odd society of wolves that lives off House Tremere. She cannot speak. Wolf is an Essential Trait: it keeps her loyal to her pack, out of reach of Hermetic magic, and proof against spells that would make her behave like a person. The book's list also names Magical Creature, left out here because it adds nothing to Magic Animal. Wound ranges: Light 1-4, Medium to 8, Heavy to 12, Incapacitated to 16.
Cords: Gold +2, Silver +1, Bronze +3. Bond powers: shared sight (ArM5 p. 105), the complex form of mental speech, and Ever-present Familiar, which calls her to Monica's side from up to seven leagues off, 24 times a day; she often fetches Arcane Connections to places for Monica's Leap of Homecoming.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal ch. 2

creatures.name: Zuban, a Four-Eyed Dog

powers.name: Dispel the Dark
powers.description: A faerie that hears his bark loses 5 Might if it penetrates; his Slow Power means he must bark for two rounds first.

creatures.appearance: A middling dog with his tail held high, tawny with white chest and paws, a black muzzle and two black spots over his eyes. He keeps walking into things, as if his eyes were on something nobody else can see.
creatures.notes: A sabotnik dog: anyone born on a Saturday is safe from the direct powers of vampires that cannot harm the Saturday-born, and such dogs are known by the black marks over their eyes. Ferocity 1 (3). He makes a magical animal companion, or a grog if his Cunning becomes Intelligence. Wound ranges: Light 1-3, Medium to 6, Heavy to 9, Incapacitated to 12, Dead from 13.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal ch. 9

creatures.name: Saint Ivan Rilski

powers.name: Strike Dumb
powers.description: Leaves the target wholly mute until the saint chooses to lift it.

creatures.appearance: Shown with the Holy Cross and a scroll or open book written in Cyrillic letters.
creatures.notes:
John of Rila, the patron of Bulgaria: a hermit, healer and mystic who died in 946 after twelve years in a cave, three in a hollow oak and seven on a high rock above the cave, where his followers grew into the monastery of Rila. The cave, the tree and the rock have a Divine aura of 4, apart from the monastery's Dominion of 3; his body, still uncorrupted, lies in Tarnovo. Venerated by the Bulgarians, the people of Sredets and Tarnovo, monks and hermits; his feast is 19 October. Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Expel Demons, The Faithful Made Whole and Grant of Serenity.
The monks speak for him and carry weight in Bulgarian politics. Before they help, they may ask petitioners to repeat his ordeal in miniature, twelve days in the cave, three in the oak and seven on the rock, while he weighs their purity of purpose; those who pass may gain the monastery as an ally, and a like ordeal could initiate a Holy Tradition of the saint.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal ch. 4

lexander.name: Lexander
lexander.summary:
Radomir's filius, looking forty-one, and a cives (of Coeris). He believes Laniena exists to train soldiers for House Tremere, and wants the Hunters' Arts stretched to every supernatural enemy the Order might face, but has neither the skill nor the knowledge to do it, so he nags Murat the Younger to; he has more than once floated 'Hermetic magus' as a Foe Art for hunting the Marched. Murat will not let him see his pater's scripts, so every recruit must pass through Murat's hands.

He drills the Fectores without end against both steel and spells, catching monsters and setting them loose in the caves for his pupils to hunt, often at mortal risk. A master of Rego, above all with Vim, Corpus and Animal.

links.note: Sodalis and constant rival; wants Murat's scripts

murat_the_younger.name: Murat the Younger
murat_the_younger.summary:
A Hermetic Fector, the youngest of Murat of Terezin's three apprentices, who took his master's name at his Gauntlet; he looks forty-two. A hospes (of Diodorus), whose own agreement lets him take apprentices without the Praeco's leave, so that he trains as many as he can for the Tremere war machine.

He is fascinated by the hunters of each region and often travels to chase word of a new way to fight vampires or ward off witches. He teaches his pupils the Ban Art above all, to give them a chance of living through Lexander's exercises, which only angers Lexander more. He holds his pater's initiation scripts.

oeagrus.name: Oeagrus
oeagrus.summary:
The senior Orphic magus of the Tribunal, looking sixty-eight, who fancies himself head of the whole Cult, with no grounds at all. Unlike most of the Cult he worships Orpheus openly as a god, which has won him no friends among the Tremere. He thinks the Cult on Lesbos has Orpheus's head and is keeping it from him. He is mad: the Cult tends to call it divine madness, everyone else plain lunacy. He hates women.

Outsiders seldom see him. He goes about in a loincloth, careless of his looks, his hair wild and twigs caught in his tangled beard.
oeagrus.secrets: His treasure is the mummified arm of Orpheus, whom the Maenads tore apart; he seeks a way to rebuild the god by grafting the dismembered body onto himself.

bozhidar.name: Bozhidar
bozhidar.summary:
The music teacher at Gela, looking thirty-eight, who usually has two or three pupils. His Study Bonus has made him strong in Imaginem from what his students bring, and he now needs ever finer musicians to learn from.

A good-looking man with dark curls and an easy smile, thickening round the middle since the village's unmarried women began bringing him honey cakes.

yekaterina.name: Yekaterina
yekaterina.summary:
Evredika's aedile, the latest of a line, looking thirty-two. Oeagrus usually sours each 'Tremere overseer', as he calls them, enough that they ask to leave after a decade or so, and he takes a woman in the post as a double insult from the House. She means, for now, to stay, and from her lonely sanctum in the Devil's Throat has deepened her study of necromancy.

Slender and fair, she wears a mask made of a skull, which she has begun to turn into her talisman.

benilda.name: Benilda
benilda.summary:
Chief Quaesitor of the Tribunal and leader of Seuthopolis, a head of the Transitionalists in House Guernicus. She thinks the Tremere may be right that the way magi live is going to change, which will test those who keep justice hard, and innovates in law to ready her House. She specialises in investigation and keeps the Red and Black Libraries.

The Traditionalists call her brand of Transitionalism collusion with House Tremere to bend the Code, but can do little against her while Tremere backs her: without Tremere arms the Quaesitors would struggle to make Autumn covenants elsewhere obey the Code. She thought it feeble of the Prima of Guernicus to give up reconciling the factions and send them to fight case by case at Tribunal; but since that is the war now, with the Order's future at stake, she will play politics as ruthlessly as any Traditionalist.

She presides at Tribunal, witnesses oaths and binds contracts into the Peripheral Code; accusations are laid before her, and she is the Quaesitor characters meet for the Tribunal's business.

caledonia.name: Caledonia
caledonia.summary:
The older Quaesitor sent where things are dangerous, raised (as her name says) in the Loch Leglean Tribunal. She has an odd faerie blood, that of the Washerwoman of the Ford, which shows her visions of her own possible death and her foes'. Her investigative spells are weak, but in Wizard's War she is skilful and unpredictable, and her speciality is magical self-defence.

Met on her investigations, she can ask any magus for all reasonable help: lodging and supplies, and often companions and grogs with local knowledge or useful skills. She attends every Wizard's March. She seeks friends among the Merinita, thought partial in Scotland but of no matter here.

saturnino.name: Saturnino

personality_traits.name: Determined to do evil by doing what others call good

saturnino.summary:
Marshal of Transylvania: House Guernicus's chief hoplite in the Tribunal, the senior lictor and leader of Wizard's Marches; his age is unknown. He is one of the elders of the Path of Strife, Criamon extremists who do evil so that their Housemates may stay clean, and who, unlike other Criamon, plunge into the world to dirty themselves. His House's notion of evil is so strange that he usually seems a very ordinary magus: eating meat is evil, and so is having a wife, and he does both.

Only slowly do others see that he finds no moral difference between a bacon pie and burning a child, and would do either if it were needed. He knows right from wrong and, without remorse, picks wrong when it must be done, so others need not; but he does no pointless cruelty, will not deal with demons, which he thinks personal weakness, and will not betray his sect or his wife, since that would be right. He kills magi well and, in his own odd terms, can be relied on. He is still a Criamon, with riddles, strange quests and errands to magical places, only more often bloody to the elbows. He excels at surprising foes and at mystical swordplay.
saturnino.secrets: He serves here because he thinks gathering the Red and Black Libraries was a deep error, and because he wonders whether the Tribunal's strange faeries come of the Criamon having stolen the World Tree.

scipio.name: Scipio
scipio.summary:
The mediator, skilled in talk and Mentem magic. At Tribunal each side argues and the rest vote, so Tremere's opponents always lose and Tremere wins only by making enemies; with Scipio between them a magus can settle with another magus or an oppidum without forcing the House to take sides. He would like a posting to a Tribunal where, without someone like him, blood might be shed; his superiors agree he will be useful there one day, but want him to keep honing his skills first, since there the smallest slip could be costly.

The easiest of the four Quaesitors to approach: gentle in manner, less strict about the letter of the law, and willing to give legal advice. He can sometimes calm a quarrel between the characters and someone they have angered, though they may have to give ground.

terencia.name: Terencia
terencia.summary:
A lictor on Caledonia's team and the oppidum's aedile, a young maga trained as a military scout, whose magic carries her fast through a country and weighs its dangers. She was put with Caledonia because the Quaesitor lacks many investigative spells; she is no great fighter, but Caledonia is far deadlier than most Quaesitors and her fellow lictor Saturnino is among the Order's most feared. She hopes a turn with the Quaesitors will help her to a posting abroad later.

A Rego Corpus specialist with, like many of her House, some Terram, she wants her talisman to be a trophy of a famous case she helps Caledonia crack. Knowing she needs friends among young magi, and wanting some her own age, she is easy to approach and can help characters against their foes; she loves the work but never seems to have time to herself.

vigilia.name: Vigilia
vigilia.summary:
A bitter old maga whom nothing magi do to each other surprises any more. Her spells find out what magi have done without breaking the Code, and she specialises in spying on magi. She always goes with two hoplites strong enough to cut her free of a camp that is in on a plot: dark Merinita once ambushed her and took both her legs, and though she regrew them with Corpus vis, seeing two suspects eat her feet made her careful.

She is the only working Quaesitor of the Tribunal censured for breaking the Code, for spying on a magus by accident while casting without force; she kept her place because her accuser asked for mercy, but may no longer investigate the Histrian oppida, where she cannot seem neutral. Characters are right to distrust her, and she is becoming a problem for her House, but she is good at reading and undoing magical defences. She is called to judge whether a magus died in his laboratory, and to assess ancient magical sites.

nestor.name: Nestor
nestor.summary:
Curator of Tablinum since 1170, looking forty-eight: tall and bone-thin, in a monk's habit dyed bright yellow, walking with a quick, jerky, insect-like stride. His sigil is a tic of teleportation, made far worse by his Twilights: he vanishes and reappears an instant later half a step away.

He affects to live apart from Tribunal politics, as for years he truly did, but for a decade he has feared that other Tremere are plotting against him, though he has found no plot. He knows that finding none may mean he is going mad, and since there might be a plot he dares tell no one of either fear. He may be both mad and the target of a plot.

He studies what he believes is the drift of regiones against one another: Leap of Homecoming, he says, takes a tiny, measurable time that depends on the levels left and reached and changes from trip to trip, and a great brass orrery in his laboratory, whose spheres are regiones, plots their motion. He has found no use for it, may be quite wrong, and will not raise the subject, but will eagerly compare notes with a magus who does.

demetrius.name: Demetrius
demetrius.summary:
Tablinum's aedile, trained in the Theban Tribunal, young, keen to learn and fluent in Latin, Greek and Arabic. Born Basem in the Saracen lands, he was cast out by his village for his Blatant Gift and was living like a beast in the waste when a Bonisagus Seeker passing by found him. He now understands his Gift and bears his family no grudge, but abandonment left him desperate to please new friends: he knows it and tries not to act like an anxious puppy, though he usually sees how foolish he looked only after some pleading offer is made.

His sigil is a faint pop, as if something small left the world, louder as his spells grow stronger. He spends long hours fixing the catalogues, shamefully wrong in his view, and means to send copies to the other Tribunals, since sharing knowledge was Bonisagus's vision; he suspects the others here do not agree.

theodora.name: Theodora
theodora.summary:
Theodore's twin, looking twenty-eight. Nestor took in the twins as bawling infants and hid them with two nurses in a secret regio until their Gifts could be Opened and he could claim them as apprentices. Theodora is noisy, her hair long and matted and her habits filthy, and screams, spits and throws things when crossed, yet she forgets slights quickly and bears with the beast in everyone. She took her longevity potion in her early twenties out of vanity and soon rued the barrenness it brought.

Her magic, like her laboratory, is showy and reckless: she keeps tipping new ingredients, seemingly at random, into an ever-boiling cauldron, which she swears improves her magic, and her laboratory does often turn out work beyond her.

theodore.name: Theodore
theodore.summary:
Theodora's twin, though looking sixty he could pass for her father. He hardly speaks except to the two nurses who raised them, now old women in their seventies, one almost blind and one bedridden, who still live in the nursery regio. He never raises his voice and keeps himself, his clothes and his laboratory spotless, with grogs guarding its door in shifts; he spends hours gazing at the still pool at its heart.

His ideas are strange. He thinks body hair breeds disease and keeps himself hairless by magic, and he put off his longevity potion until fifty, perhaps only to mock his sister.

accursius_adiran.name: Accursius Adiran
accursius_adiran.summary:
The chief Mercere: an aged magus who leads the Histrian magi and the Tribunal's Redcaps after a fashion. He has great standing and decides which Redcaps get longevity rituals, but cannot really make the sprawling family obey; long since reconciled to that, he steers it through yearly meetings of the heads of the main families. He works at craftwork and illusion.

Too old to travel without magic, he keeps to his laboratory, at Shrouded Bay because it is nicer, though his lab there is worse than the one he leaves to Volante. He can send Redcap families to help, make weak longevity rituals fit for young magi, open the House's cache of items, and he collects favours to spend when a Redcap's trouble goes beyond what the Code obliges magi to fix.

Every few years the lab-bound life gets too much and he takes a holiday, famous for embarrassment, scrapes and scandal; when he vanishes, word goes round the Redcaps to watch for the Old Man and keep things quiet. He may turn up on one of these jaunts in a town near the players' oppidum.

leontine_adiran.name: Leontine Adiran
leontine_adiran.summary:
The Tribunal's chief negotiator: only thirty, yet one of the finest communicators in Mythic Europe, encouraged to grow her gift for diplomacy at the cost of her magic, a bargain she accepts gladly for now. She works in espionage, and usually travels with Merit of Tremere. Her task is to threaten, bribe and persuade, so she seeks out magi with narrow Affinities for help, and pays in introductions to the most powerful magi in this and the neighbouring Tribunals, or in the name of exactly the right person.

She is not Dominic of Tytalus's apprentice but his protégée; rumour, knowing the Tytalus, invents a passionate affair seasoned with murder attempts. In truth he enjoys a sharp, amusing pupil and she a wily mentor and something of a father. She also sharpens her wits arguing ethics with an ancient zmaj of Istria.

pahniro_adiran.name: Pahniro Adiran

personality_traits.name: Likes fooling people with his old codger act

pahniro_adiran.summary:
The aedile of Old Histria, an old Tremere near Twilight given the post as a useful retirement, since few in the House expect trouble at Histria; he is the House's eyes on this western gate. He equips mundane spies, is rumoured to run the House's agents in the Roman Tribunal, and laughs that off: surely a spymaster would live in Venice? He says he is only an old man finishing his talisman as a legacy, with Placido as his lab assistant.

Anyone breaking the Code nearby may meet him first, sizing things up before he calls the hoplites and Quaesitors. A prolific letter writer, he asks Tremere for help when he wants to look into something without alarming the Redcaps, and trades news with others for favours; coloniae often owe senior Tremere aid by their terms, so players may be bound to serve his whims. The Mercere often send him after strigons, which he passes to younger magi.
pahniro_adiran.secrets: His doddering is misdirection: he served twenty years as a hoplite and has killed three magi in single combat.

placido_adiran.name: Placido Adiran
placido_adiran.summary:
The aedile of Shrouded Bay, a young Tremere with an Affinity for Aquam who runs the House's trading fleet, keeps it ready for war, and specialises in battle magic at sea. Lately taken with naval sabotage, he has money to try new ways of fighting ships and wants partners; keeping even a small navy supplied means endless dealing with suppliers, their rivals and the local nobles, so he calls on coloniae with strategic land or odd faerie resources and on anyone with useful skills when new ports open.

He loathes pirates with startling zeal. At heart he loves fights to the death for the thrill, but will not see himself as a murderer, so he turns the urge on people everyone agrees deserve it, and invites players with a gift for mayhem or swift travel to clear pirate nests with him. He is also Pahniro's lab assistant on his talisman, a service other Houses think beneath a magus but the Tremere do not.

priscilla_of_verditius.name: Priscilla of Verditius

personality_traits.name: Wants to do her own thing

priscilla_of_verditius.summary:
A maga of middle years who spends most of her time at Old Histria brewing longevity potions for the unGifted, a waste of her talent, she thinks. She has quarrelled with her teacher, yet has neither the wish to join a frontier oppidum nor the political skill to win better terms; she will not call herself Adiran, feeling she does not belong, and longs for a workshop to make magical puppets in peace.

She hates discussing her rote work, but is a treasure for anyone founding a colonia: she knows the local law and custom, the sites of local legend, and the promising places the Tribunal's survey has marked for settlement, and though her ties to senior magi are weak, she knows whom to ask.

volante_adiran.name: Volante Adiran
volante_adiran.summary:
A Gifted Mercere from Italy, likely to follow Accursius when he dies or fades into Twilight, though she has even less hold on the local family than he does. Her recent marriage to a man of an old Redcap line made her less of a stranger, but pulls her from her work of putting right what goes wrong for the family; the couple live in Accursius's fine suite and laboratory at Old Histria. She is skilled in travel and flying magic, though politics has cut into her studies.

When a Redcap is hurt or killed, she is the one who comes, and the one to report to. She effectively commands the small fighting part of the Redcap fleet and lends items that help Redcaps force a way through hard country. The senior Redcaps want her to raise an heir or two so the family gets leaders who know local ways rather than a new magus from Harco each generation; she will not take apprentices yet, which may cause friction when she succeeds. She seeks favours for her House, and a magical bird as her familiar.

merit.name: Merit
merit.summary:
An older Tremere, shaven-headed and heavily muscled, with a stare that could split masonry, who lives at the Histrian chapter house in Venice and usually goes with Leontine on her missions as the Tremere half of the Tribunal's envoys.

A member of Old Histria lodged in Venice, in the Roman Tribunal; the book gives no age or privilege.

albertus.name: Albertus
albertus.summary:
Archmagus and Praeco of Transylvania, chosen by vote with the Prima's blessing, and the magus who runs Lycaneon's work: he hands out projects, keeps them to time, commissions pieces from skilled item-makers, and is the one to see about buying or borrowing an item. An engineer by training and a Rego specialist who also favours Terram and Vim, he follows who is in the Tribunal and what they do, because building teams is his great talent.

One of the Order's youngest archmagi, he is a magnet for challengers, and his known Rego bent makes him weak at certamen. Expecting to lose challenges fast, he set his challenge as the most useful item given to House Tremere after three years' work: it puts off Verditius magi loath to part with their best, it cannot be finished in one Tribunal, the House gains a fine item even if he loses, and only a few Tremere know the whole reserve, so a rival's powerful piece may duplicate something the House already owns. He has faced one challenge and won.

He has no plan yet to seek the Prima's seat, though he expects to want it one day. As Primus he would build a network of hidden roads, coaching houses and hospitals across the Tribunal, commission spells across the Order, send Redcaps to scout and magi to clear routes, invite the best item-crafters to work, perhaps sponsor a prize at the Verdi contest, and keep the House's engineers busy for years.

arhmina.name: Arhmina
arhmina.summary:
A young Moorish sorceress from Iberia, a colona, who favours Rego and Vim. She came to Lycaneon to help House Tremere devise counterspells to her own tradition, for reasons she keeps to herself; gossip says a rival who wanted to marry her beat her in a run of magical duels, and she wants shelter first and revenge later. Her pay is a fine longevity ritual, good study books and items made to hurt that rival, and if she proves useful, Tremere help when she goes home to face him.

She means to stay no more than ten years, and to use them: raising her Arts, learning the strange spirits of the dark mountains, visiting Constantinople, maybe going on to Mecca. She works closely with Clement, and travellers may meet her on the road.

clement.name: Clement
clement.summary:
A middle-aged Tremere, trained first as a magical spy, who specialises in Mentem spells for battle and is a necromancer; he favours Rego, Perdo, Mentem and Vim. He was called back to Lycaneon for the Prima's plan to carry the House's power into the Levant, and is researching how to sway the minds of the spirits Arab sorcerers draw on.

He wants to meet Muslim magicians to find more simple wards against such spirits, works closely with Arhmina, and spends time in the Muslim towns the King of Hungary founded for his officials, where folk magicians driven out of the Levant will happily work for Christians. His spells so far use two ideas: the spirits shun the name of God as Muslims say it, which strong Creo Imaginem can carry far, and many djinn are said to be of smokeless fire, so bitter cold outside their Magic Resistance may hurt them. He is no hand at that second kind of magic and would welcome a partner who is.

phillip.name: Phillip
phillip.summary:
A young Herbam specialist known for spells that build and keep siege engines, who favours Muto, Rego, Herbam and Terram. He is testing, with scale models in big tanks in his huge laboratory, which magically made woods best suit magical shipbuilding: not a new question, but he is painfully thorough. Samples of rare wood are precious to him, since studying one makes the species easier to copy by magic. His findings will go to the group of Tremere working to make ships a reliable platform for magi in battle.

He holds an arcane connection to Leviathan, the House's mothballed Adriatic naval base, and would move there if a sea war came; with his skill and its yards, the House would lack crews, not hulls. He is often at Shrouded Bay working on the Tremere and Mercere fleets. He dreams of a naval base in the Hungarian mountains, reached through the passages he believes join the Tribunal's lakes to the sea, and would lead an expedition into one if he could.

zalmoxis.name: Zalmoxis
zalmoxis.summary:
Archmagus, a hospes, the senior Verditius in the Tribunal, who has worked at Lycaneon for more than forty years. He specialises in Corpus, above all healing on the battlefield and curing disease, and in longevity potions and rituals. He bears a local pagan god's name but has nothing to do with the old cult.

The Tremere need him: their focus on certamen leaves none of them with a magical focus fit for longevity work, so they buy the lesser rituals from young Verditius and the best from Corpus experts in other Tribunals for their senior magi. The House always keeps at least one such expert close, so that in an Order-wide crisis it can still train healers and extenders of life.

simium_arileins.name: Simium Arileins
simium_arileins.summary:
The school's eldest magus and its headmaster, known across the Order as a historian and philosopher and a tireless author of beginners' texts on many subjects, the Arts among them, found as far off as Stonehenge and Iberia, though mostly fit only for young magi. He looks fifty-eight.

Years at the lectern have bent his back, and his small dark eyes blink constantly; he dresses in plain black robes and a black skullcap. His heartbeast is a raven bigger than a man, through the Mystery of the Inner Heartbeast, and his flights over the mountains have bred local tales of a demon bird that can carry off a grown man.

andrew_melanchthon.name: Andrew Melanchthon
andrew_melanchthon.summary:
A Tremere who left the Rhine Tribunal after loud public quarrels with a leading Bonisagus branded him an empiricist and an atheist and ended any hope of office there. The charge of atheism is unjust: like most Tremere he is impious, not godless; his real offence was saying aloud that God is no loving father. He looks thirty-six.

The Scholomance lets him teach his own course: moral philosophy and rhetoric from texts the establishment calls heretical or blasphemous. He dreams of pupils carrying his humanist programme into Europe's universities and courts.

poena.name: Poena
poena.summary:
Prima of House Tremere these two years, and arguably the most powerful magus in Mythic Europe in politics: slight and stern, silver-haired, with a perfect memory. She holds every entry of the Book of Legacies in her head, knows every Tremere by name and roughly what each is doing, and fits her exarchs' and spies' reports together into elaborate designs. She favours Intellego, Muto, Imaginem and Mentem.

She governs the whole House, but quietly, through her secretaries, councillors, exarchs and legata. She always wants new pieces for her plans, unlike those she has, so magi from outside the House who act predictably are valuable to her; she holds the key to the richest stores in Europe and likely knows what the player characters want, or where to find it.

angiola.name: Angiola
angiola.summary:
Young, fair and sharp-tongued, a maga with the Gentle Gift whom Poena uses to speak for her to those the Gift unsettles. Trained as an Assessor, she wears strong illusions that make her seem older and male, the better to be believed, and the world grows sharper around her when she casts. She favours Muto and Imaginem, with some Creo and Mentem.

She tidies up trouble between magi and mundanes in the Tribunal, so she is the one who comes when characters have badly failed among mortals, and she checks on any who pass themselves off as nobles. She is Janus's chief aide.

dominic_of_tytalus.name: Dominic of Tytalus
dominic_of_tytalus.summary:
Archmagus and the aedile of Coeris, a hospes: the Tytalus who has set himself to read and forestall the schemes of every other Tytalus and warn the Tremere, a deadly serious game against his whole House. He believes his House badly underrates the Tremere, who once, in the Corruption, crushed it like an egg, and fears that their patience with Tytalus baiting may give way now that the Theban Tribunal's weakness leaves them magi to spare.

Very tall, black-clad down to his skullcap, with a devilish beard he knows looks overdone, which is the point; his sigil, a thunderclap, he privately finds funny. He favours weather magic and is a skilled necromancer. Close to the Prima but no Tremere, he always needs favours against some Tytalus plot and repays them with contacts, devious counsel and necromantic mayhem. Leontine of Tytalus of Old Histria is his protégé.

horatius.name: Horatius
horatius.summary:
Secretary for operations, seeing through what the last Decennial planned; under some Primi this post was mighty, but Poena's own grip on resources leaves him less, and he keeps things running and reports what goes wrong. Young for so high a post and plump for a Tremere, he worked beside Poena before her rise, helped arrange her succession, and is her husband's brother. A Signaler by training with his own sigil, comforting warmth; he favours Creo, Rego, Imaginem and Terram.

He seldom leaves Coeris, but magi abroad write to him with proposals, as the manager of House business; he is easier to reach than Poena and can arrange to see her. He does not seek the Primacy but would be a fine compromise if the House split, and would ring the north and east shores of the Black Sea with oppida to make it a Hermetic lake.

janus.name: Janus
janus.summary:
Secretary for contingencies: he keeps the House's stockpiles and asks for Tremere, or magi of the oppida, to be trained in odd skills in case one of his unlikely events comes to pass. Raised in the Rhineland, muscular and handsome, chaste and aloof with attractive women; his sigil is ribbons of scarlet light. He favours Creo, Intellego, Rego and above all Mentem, a well-known speciality that weakens him in certamen, and is a spiritual necromancer with a gift for spycraft and the Visions Flaw. He was secretary for operations under the previous Primus.

He watches characters whose doings might, however remotely, start a crisis, and quietly sets counterweights; years later he may call on skills he had them learn, to untangle a crisis born of several unlikely chances at once.
janus.secrets: Janus suffers a lycanthropy that magic can hold back and that changes only his shape, not his mind. He is ashamed of it and keeps it secret, so he will never seek the Primacy, and it passes by intercourse, hence his coldness to women.

isaac_of_merinita.name: Isaac of Merinita
isaac_of_merinita.summary:
Coeris's expert on faeries, a cives, left deeply disturbed if not mad by the Tribunal's dark faeries; his mood swings from cheer to gloom without warning. He looks forty but has spent years in Faerie, so his true age is unknown. His skewed view and his hatred and vast knowledge of vampiric faeries make him Tatiana's adviser; she values his knack for surviving anything, if not always whole. He prefers gloomy faerie magic.

Frail-looking, yet his faerie blood makes him strong and nimble. Scars as if torn by madmen's teeth mark his wrists, ankles, neck and thighs, which Hermetic magic cannot heal, from a faerie curse or torture that harmed his Essential Nature. His sigil is the smell of burning pine cones, though he says it was not always so.

juturnus.name: Juturnus
juturnus.summary:
Horatius's troubleshooter, sent to find out why something in the House's operations went wrong and to put it right. Cocky, skilled and quick to violence, he is unlike a bureaucratic Tremere and may have risen too fast. Small objects near him arrange themselves into geometric shapes. He favours Rego, with some Perdo and Intellego, Animal and Terram.

He is black and athletic; decades ago a Primus had the Redcaps find Gifted Arab and African children, thinking they could work less conspicuously in Arab lands, and he was one of them. Like many he trained first as an Assessor, a kind of spy, and has since learnt more widely. The book gives no privilege for him.

tatiana.name: Tatiana
tatiana.summary:
Secretary for emergencies and Poena's spymistress: she warns the House of trouble ahead and finds answers when it is caught off guard. Of a Szekler family she has not seen since her apprenticeship; she turns briefly invisible whenever she casts, to her irritation. She favours Creo, Muto, Herbam and Corpus, and Isaac assists her.

She appears when something dreadful is close, takes over the characters' help and resources, and sends them into the worst of it to buy the House and Order time; magi who refuse her are tarnished for good in some circles.
tatiana.secrets: Tatiana secretly belongs to the Keepers of the Silence of the Temple, a small, unofficial society named for the man who burnt the temple of Artemis at Ephesus to be famous and whose name was then forbidden. They hold that Tytalus magi too often do monstrous, foolish things for fame, and set out to destroy such vandals, then their memory.

essedarius.name: Essedarius
essedarius.summary:
Leader of Kezdö Válasz since 1215 and the fourth in its history, filius of Macrobius, filius of Gasparus, filius of the founder Norsius; a cives (of Coeris). Tall, thickset and bald, with brown eyes, he looks thirty-eight and at ease, wears dark clothes for the saddle, and never goes without his talisman, an enchanted sword holding several powers to wound and to act at a distance. A Corpus specialist, he has not aged a day since his first longevity ritual.

Born in the Order, son of a warrior of Laniena, schooled at the Scholomance, he has known no life outside House Tremere; a steady rather than a brilliant pupil, he was picked as Macrobius's apprentice. When an angry griffin met by chance tore Macrobius apart in 1215, he took the lead.

Untested so far, he watches the growing quarrel between Bosnia and Hungary and dreads the slaughter a crusade would bring; he knows the Hungarian knights who cross the border to kill Patarians, tells his agents to keep clear of them, and will protect his Bosnian spies. To show his commitment he lives in the field, in a camp with six armed grogs, rather than in his fort; some say he should be in his lab instead. He has given Adulio a magic bridle that calms a horse so it will carry a magus.

leona.name: Leona
leona.summary:
Essedarius's partner, who took the place of her old partner Macrobius; a cives (of Coeris), looking fifty-six. Of middle height and stout, in riding clothes like most of her sodales, she is a master of Herbam who learns what she needs by questioning the trees and bushes wherever she goes; her sigil is a scent of lilac, stronger the greater the spell. People take her for slow and heavy, but she is quick to act and quicker to anger. She made many of the oppidum's signal charms.

She was not with Macrobius when the griffin killed him and still blames herself; killing that beast did not cool her rage, and she hunts griffins still, roaming the southern Dinaric Alps and the Prokletije, where he fell, and has built a fort there.

adulio.name: Adulio
adulio.summary:
A cives (of Coeris), looking thirty-six, who joined in 1204, two months after the Latins took Constantinople: the fall, at the end of his apprenticeship, convinced him Transylvania was in danger too, and he means to spare it what crusaders did to the Theban Tribunal. Thin as a reed and dark-haired, he looks ready for violence at any moment, and his familiar, a restless Eurasian lynx called Ucigas ('Killer' in Romanian), adds to the effect. He favours destructive Auram spells.

Sixteen years with no great threat have disappointed him; brushes with giants have not sated him. The loudest warmonger in the oppidum, he sees danger everywhere, and the Quaesitors have censured him twice, once for needlessly provoking local faeries and once for deliberately killing a band of Latin knights raiding out of Epirus; neither changed him. A horse breeder's son with an eye for good mounts, he rides with a magic bridle Essedarius made.

neculai.name: Neculai
neculai.summary:
The oppidum's aedile and a socius (of Domostron), though the book also says every member is a cives; he looks thirty-nine. Born in the Carpathian foothills of Hungary, he was found by a wandering Bjornaer and raised and apprenticed in the Stonehenge Tribunal; once gauntleted he longed for home and asked several Transylvanian oppida to take him, and Kezdö Válasz, short of an aedile, took him at once, an offer he accepted without enthusiasm. Small, hawk-like and beak-nosed, with hair so black it looks blue, he is an Intellego specialist who can talk to nearly any bird, beast or fish. His heartbeast is a pern, the honey buzzard, and he travels on the wing.

He belongs to Clan Sirnas, the Bjornaer guardians, who distrust House Tremere and expect him to report on it. He resents that nearly as much as being paired with Adulio, and will not spy on anyone: he keeps the Gathering of Twelve Years' business to himself but tells his sodales he may speak there of what he has seen, and has attended twice since joining. Essedarius shrugs: the Tremere have nothing to hide and the Bjornaer nothing to fear. Essedarius has now sent him to visit Leona in the Prokletije, to keep her informed and to keep an eye on her.
